## 1.5 (Optional) Neutral simulations
This adds a neutral reference for the gene's location correlations. Enable it with
`run_neutral_sim: true` in config.yaml; Snakemake prepares the subset VCFs and
passes the same toggle as `RUN_NEUTRAL_SIM`. The gene analysis runs without it.

```{r neutral_model_functions, include=FALSE}
RUN_NEUTRAL_SIM <- toupper(trimws(Sys.getenv("RUN_NEUTRAL_SIM", unset = "FALSE")))
if (!RUN_NEUTRAL_SIM %in% c("TRUE", "FALSE")) {
  stop("RUN_NEUTRAL_SIM must be TRUE or FALSE")
}
RUN_NEUTRAL_SIM <- as.logical(RUN_NEUTRAL_SIM)
# The full pool is a reference, not a target for matched-size subsets of itself.
if (neutral_reference) RUN_NEUTRAL_SIM <- FALSE

if (RUN_NEUTRAL_SIM) {
  neutral_plan_path <- Sys.getenv("NEUTRAL_PLAN", unset = "")
  neutral_metadata_path <- Sys.getenv("NEUTRAL_PLAN_METADATA", unset = "")
  neutral_prepared_manifest_path <- Sys.getenv("NEUTRAL_PREPARED_MANIFEST", unset = "")
  if (!compute_genetic_diversity_statistics || !all(file.exists(c(neutral_plan_path,
      neutral_metadata_path, neutral_prepared_manifest_path)))) {
    stop("Neutral simulations need location statistics and existing plan/metadata/prepared VCF files")
  }

  validate_extreme_value_percentiles <- function(percentiles) {
    percentiles <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(percentiles))
    if (any(!is.finite(percentiles)) ||
        any(percentiles <= 0 | percentiles >= 100)) {
      stop("Neutral reference percentiles must be numbers strictly between 0 and 100")
    }
    # The same six-decimal convention is used for output field names in Python.
    percentiles <- round(percentiles, 6)
    if (any(percentiles <= 0 | percentiles >= 100) || anyDuplicated(percentiles)) {
      stop("Neutral reference percentiles must be distinct at six-decimal precision")
    }
    percentiles
  }

  neutral_percentile_labels <- function(percentiles) {
    vapply(validate_extreme_value_percentiles(percentiles), function(p) {
      label <- sub("\\.?0+$", "", sprintf("%.6f", p))
      label
    }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  }

  neutral_percentile_fields <- function(percentiles, prefix) {
    labels <- neutral_percentile_labels(percentiles)
    if (!length(labels)) return(character())
    paste0(prefix, "q", gsub(".", "_", labels, fixed = TRUE))
  }

  neutral_tail <- function(observed, null, requested, min_valid_fraction = 0.9,
                           extreme_value_percentiles = c(95, 99)) {
    extreme_value_percentiles <- validate_extreme_value_percentiles(extreme_value_percentiles)
    null <- abs(null[is.finite(null)])
    n <- length(null)
    status <- if (!is.finite(observed)) "undefined_observed_correlation" else if (
      n < ceiling(requested * min_valid_fraction)) "too_few_valid_replicates" else "ok"
    p <- if (status == "ok") (1 + sum(null >= abs(observed) - 1e-12)) / (n + 1) else NA_real_
    # Quantiles describe the reference distribution; they are not p-values.
    # Interpolation and the add-one tail score need not have identical boundaries.
    cutoffs <- if (!length(extreme_value_percentiles)) numeric() else if (status == "ok")
      unname(stats::quantile(null, extreme_value_percentiles / 100)) else
      rep(NA_real_, length(extreme_value_percentiles))
    c(list(status = status, n = n, p = p, median = if (n) median(null) else NA_real_),
      setNames(as.list(cutoffs), neutral_percentile_fields(extreme_value_percentiles, "")))
  }

  compare_neutral_locations <- function(observed, predictors, null_gd, requested, min_valid_fraction = 0.9,
                                        extreme_value_percentiles = c(95, 99)) {
    extreme_value_percentiles <- validate_extreme_value_percentiles(extreme_value_percentiles)
    if (nrow(null_gd) != length(observed)) stop("Neutral and observed location counts differ")
    result <- list()
    replicate_rows <- list()
    for (variable in names(predictors)) {
      x <- predictors[[variable]]
      if (length(x) != length(observed)) stop("Predictor and location counts differ")
      # Freeze the observed complete-case mask. Replicates cannot select easier locations.
      keep <- is.finite(observed) & is.finite(x)
      obs <- location_association(observed[keep], x[keep])
      r <- rho <- rep(NA_real_, ncol(null_gd))
      if (sum(keep) >= 3 && sd(x[keep]) > 0) {
        for (b in seq_len(ncol(null_gd))) {
          y <- null_gd[keep, b]
          if (all(is.finite(y)) && sd(y) > 0) {
            r[b] <- cor(x[keep], y, method = "pearson")
            rho[b] <- cor(x[keep], y, method = "spearman")
          }
        }
      }
      pearson <- neutral_tail(obs$r, r, requested, min_valid_fraction, extreme_value_percentiles)
      spearman <- neutral_tail(obs$rho, rho, requested, min_valid_fraction, extreme_value_percentiles)
      cutoff_names <- neutral_percentile_fields(extreme_value_percentiles, "")
      result[[variable]] <- list(n_locations = obs$n, p_neutral = pearson$p,
        p_neutral_rho = spearman$p, neutral_n_valid = pearson$n,
        neutral_n_valid_rho = spearman$n, neutral_abs_r_median = pearson$median,
        neutral_status = pearson$status,
        neutral_rho_status = spearman$status)
      result[[variable]] <- c(result[[variable]],
        setNames(pearson[cutoff_names], neutral_percentile_fields(extreme_value_percentiles, "neutral_abs_r_")),
        setNames(spearman[cutoff_names], neutral_percentile_fields(extreme_value_percentiles, "neutral_abs_rho_")))
      replicate_rows[[variable]] <- data.frame(variable = variable, replicate = seq_along(r),
        n_locations = obs$n, r = r, rho = rho)
    }
    list(fields = result, replicates = do.call(rbind, replicate_rows))
  }

  neutral_integer_indices <- function(indices, label = "Neutral marker indices") {
    values <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(unlist(indices, use.names = FALSE)))
    if (!length(values) || any(!is.finite(values)) || any(values < 1 | values != floor(values)) ||
        any(values > .Machine$integer.max) || anyDuplicated(values)) {
      stop(paste(label, "must be distinct positive integer record indices"))
    }
    as.integer(values)
  }

  neutral_column_indices <- function(selected, pool_indices, expected_k, pool_n_matched = Inf) {
    selected <- neutral_integer_indices(selected, "Neutral subset indices")
    pool_indices <- neutral_integer_indices(pool_indices, "Prepared VCF pool indices")
    if (length(selected) != expected_k || any(selected > pool_n_matched) ||
        any(pool_indices > pool_n_matched)) stop("Neutral subset count or pool index range is invalid")
    columns <- match(selected, pool_indices)
    if (anyNA(columns)) stop("Prepared VCF is missing SNP records required by the neutral plan")
    columns
  }

  check_neutral_fingerprint <- function(path, expected, label) {
    if (length(expected) != 1L || !is.character(expected) ||
        !grepl("^[a-fA-F0-9]{32}$", expected) || !file.exists(path) ||
        !identical(unname(tools::md5sum(path)), tolower(expected))) {
      stop(paste(label, "is missing or stale; regenerate neutral preparation"))
    }
  }

  neutral_prepared_inventory <- function(manifest, manifest_path, plan_path, target_path, expected_pool_md5,
                                          status, requested, pool_n_matched = Inf) {
    check_neutral_fingerprint(plan_path, manifest$plan_md5, "Prepared subset plan")
    check_neutral_fingerprint(target_path, manifest$gene_vcf_md5, "Prepared target VCF")
    # Preparation verified the full pool. R consumes the frozen prepared VCFs and
    # verifies those files, avoiding another whole-genome scan for every report.
    if (length(expected_pool_md5) != 1L || !is.character(expected_pool_md5) ||
        !grepl("^[a-fA-F0-9]{32}$", expected_pool_md5) ||
        !identical(manifest$pool_md5, expected_pool_md5)) {
      stop("Prepared neutral pool provenance differs from subset plan")
    }
    if (!identical(manifest$status, status)) stop("Prepared VCF status differs from subset plan")
    if (length(manifest$n_technical_replicates) != 1L ||
        !is.numeric(manifest$n_technical_replicates) ||
        !is.finite(manifest$n_technical_replicates) ||
        manifest$n_technical_replicates < 0 ||
        manifest$n_technical_replicates != floor(manifest$n_technical_replicates)) {
      stop("Prepared technical replicate count must be a nonnegative integer")
    }
    if (status != "ok") {
      if (manifest$n_technical_replicates != 0 || length(manifest$vcfs) || length(manifest$replicate_files)) {
        stop("Unavailable neutral plan must not contain prepared VCF files")
      }
      return(list(entries = list(), replicate_files = character()))
    }
    if (manifest$n_technical_replicates != requested) {
      stop("Prepared VCF count differs from requested technical replicates")
    }
    if (!length(manifest$vcfs)) stop("Prepared manifest has no neutral VCF files")
    entries <- lapply(manifest$vcfs, function(entry) {
      filename <- entry$filename
      if (length(filename) != 1L || !is.character(filename) || !nzchar(filename) ||
          grepl("^[A-Za-z]:", filename) || startsWith(filename, "/") || startsWith(filename, "\\") ||
          any(strsplit(gsub("\\", "/", filename, fixed = TRUE), "/", fixed = TRUE)[[1]] == "..")) {
        stop("Prepared VCF filenames must be relative paths inside the manifest directory")
      }
      entry$path <- file.path(dirname(manifest_path), filename)
      check_neutral_fingerprint(entry$path, entry$md5, paste("Prepared VCF", filename))
      entry$pool_indices <- neutral_integer_indices(entry$pool_indices, "Prepared VCF pool indices")
      if (any(entry$pool_indices > pool_n_matched)) stop("Prepared VCF index exceeds neutral pool size")
      entry
    })
    filenames <- vapply(entries, function(entry) entry$filename, character(1))
    if (anyDuplicated(filenames)) stop("Duplicate prepared VCF filenames in manifest")
    names(entries) <- filenames
    replicate_files <- unlist(manifest$replicate_files, use.names = FALSE)
    if (!is.character(replicate_files) || length(replicate_files) != requested ||
        !all(replicate_files %in% filenames) || !all(filenames %in% replicate_files) ||
        length(filenames) != requested || anyDuplicated(replicate_files)) {
      stop("Prepared manifest does not cover every planned neutral replicate")
    }
    list(entries = entries, replicate_files = replicate_files)
  }

  run_neutral_model <- function(plan_path, metadata_path, target_path, vcf, samples, draws,
                                observed, predictors, gd_stat, statistic, het_fun, output_prefix,
                                min_valid_fraction = 0.9, prepared_manifest_path,
                                extreme_value_percentiles = c(95, 99)) {
    extreme_value_percentiles <- validate_extreme_value_percentiles(extreme_value_percentiles)
    metadata <- jsonlite::read_json(metadata_path, simplifyVector = TRUE)
    check_neutral_fingerprint(target_path, metadata$gene_vcf_md5, "Neutral subset plan target VCF")
    if (!is.null(metadata$plan_md5)) check_neutral_fingerprint(plan_path, metadata$plan_md5, "Neutral subset plan")
    if (metadata$n_variants != nrow(vcf@fix)) stop("Neutral plan and target variant counts differ")
    pool_n_matched <- if (!is.null(metadata$pool_n_matched)) metadata$pool_n_matched else
      metadata$n_available + metadata$n_excluded_overlap
    metadata$pool_n_matched <- pool_n_matched
    manifest <- jsonlite::read_json(prepared_manifest_path, simplifyVector = FALSE)
    inventory <- neutral_prepared_inventory(manifest, prepared_manifest_path, plan_path, target_path,
      metadata$pool_md5, metadata$status, metadata$technical_replicates_requested, pool_n_matched)
    metadata$prepared_manifest_md5 <- unname(tools::md5sum(prepared_manifest_path))
    metadata$pool_validation <- "prepared_manifest_matches_subset_plan"
    metadata$extreme_value_percentiles <- paste(neutral_percentile_labels(extreme_value_percentiles), collapse = ",")
    metadata$comparison <- "upper_tail_absolute_correlation"
    metadata$min_valid_fraction <- min_valid_fraction
    metadata$location_mask <- "observed_complete_cases_fixed_per_predictor"
    metadata$common_individual_draws <- TRUE
    metadata$gd_stat <- gd_stat
    metadata$gd_dosage_missing_policy <- if (gd_stat %in% c("tajimas_d", "theta"))
      gd_dosage_missing_policy else NA_character_
    if (metadata$status != "ok") {
      # Replace stale replicate results on a rerun with an unavailable target.
      write.table(data.frame(variable = character(), replicate = integer(),
        n_locations = integer(), r = numeric(), rho = numeric()),
        paste0(output_prefix, "_neutral_replicates.tsv"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
      write.table(data.frame(cluster_id = character(), replicate = integer(), gd = numeric()),
        paste0(output_prefix, "_neutral_locations.tsv"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
      fields <- lapply(predictors, function(x) c(list(p_neutral = NA_real_, p_neutral_rho = NA_real_,
        neutral_n_valid = 0L, neutral_n_valid_rho = 0L, neutral_abs_r_median = NA_real_,
        neutral_status = metadata$status, neutral_rho_status = metadata$status),
        setNames(as.list(rep(NA_real_, length(extreme_value_percentiles))),
          neutral_percentile_fields(extreme_value_percentiles, "neutral_abs_r_")),
        setNames(as.list(rep(NA_real_, length(extreme_value_percentiles))),
          neutral_percentile_fields(extreme_value_percentiles, "neutral_abs_rho_"))))
      return(list(fields = fields, metadata = metadata))
    }
    plan <- read.delim(plan_path, colClasses = "character", check.names = FALSE)
    if (!all(c("replicate", "marker_indices") %in% names(plan)) ||
        nrow(plan) != metadata$technical_replicates_requested ||
        !identical(plan$replicate, as.character(seq_len(nrow(plan)))) ||
        any(!grepl("^[1-9][0-9]*(,[1-9][0-9]*)*$", plan$marker_indices))) {
      stop("Incomplete or malformed neutral subset plan")
    }
    indices <- lapply(strsplit(plan$marker_indices, ",", fixed = TRUE), neutral_integer_indices)
    if (any(lengths(indices) != metadata$n_variants) ||
        any(unlist(indices, use.names = FALSE) > pool_n_matched)) stop("Invalid neutral subset count or pool index range")
    # Canonicalize the chr prefix exactly as the preparation stage does.
    positions <- function(fix) paste(sub("^chr", "", fix[, "CHROM"], ignore.case = TRUE),
                                     fix[, "POS"], sep = ":")
    overlap_positions <- positions(vcf@fix)
    read_matrix <- function(path, pool_indices) {
      pool_vcf <- vcfR::read.vcfR(path, verbose = FALSE)
      if (nrow(pool_vcf@fix) != length(pool_indices)) stop("Prepared VCF and manifest record counts differ")
      if (any(positions(pool_vcf@fix) %in% overlap_positions)) stop("Prepared neutral VCF overlaps target positions")
      pool_samples <- colnames(pool_vcf@gt)[-1]
      if (anyDuplicated(pool_samples) || anyDuplicated(samples) || !all(samples %in% pool_samples)) {
        stop("Neutral VCF sample IDs do not match the target")
      }
      pool_vcf <- pool_vcf[, c(1L, match(samples, pool_samples) + 1L)]
      # Conversion still uses het_fun ONLY for Ho; the converter's explicit if/else uses dosage for pi, richness, theta and D.
      # The same checks and encoding are applied to observed and neutral VCFs after sample reordering.
      x <- gd_input_from_vcf(pool_vcf, gd_stat, samples, het_fun)
      if (nrow(x) != length(samples) || ncol(x) != length(pool_indices)) {
        stop("Neutral genotype matrix dimensions differ from prepared VCF")
      }
      x
    }
    null_gd <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = length(observed), ncol = length(indices))
    # Load one k-SNP VCF per technical replicate; retain only the location results.
    for (b in seq_along(indices)) {
      entry <- inventory$entries[[inventory$replicate_files[b]]]
      if (length(entry$pool_indices) != metadata$n_variants) stop("Prepared replicate VCF has the wrong SNP count")
      i <- neutral_column_indices(indices[[b]], entry$pool_indices, metadata$n_variants, pool_n_matched)
      x <- read_matrix(entry$path, entry$pool_indices)
      null_gd[, b] <- location_gd_from_draws(x[, i, drop = FALSE], draws, statistic,
        na.rm = gd_stat %in% c("tajimas_d", "theta"))
      rm(x)
    }
    comparison <- compare_neutral_locations(observed, predictors, null_gd, nrow(plan), min_valid_fraction,
                                            extreme_value_percentiles)
    write.table(comparison$replicates, paste0(output_prefix, "_neutral_replicates.tsv"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, na = "NA")
    per_location <- data.frame(cluster_id = rep(names(draws), times = ncol(null_gd)),
      replicate = rep(seq_len(ncol(null_gd)), each = nrow(null_gd)), gd = as.vector(null_gd))
    write.table(per_location, paste0(output_prefix, "_neutral_locations.tsv"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, na = "NA")
    list(fields = comparison$fields, metadata = metadata)
  }
}
```

# 2. Raster Creation
## 2.1 Sample-driven raster, world CRS, no named-region boundary
Mollweide, not the wingen vignette's Goode Homolosine: Goode Homolosine
is interrupted specifically to keep landmasses whole, which means its
cuts land in the ocean instead - not ideal for a marine dataset.
Mollweide is uninterrupted and equal-area, at the cost of more shape
distortion far from the map's center. That trade-off is acceptable here
specifically because of the masking in section 4 below - nothing is
allowed to interpolate far enough for the distortion to matter.
```{r world-crs}
world_crs <- "+proj=moll"
```
```{r sample-points}
coords_v  <- vect(coords_file_df, geom = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = "EPSG:4326")
coords_v_mollweide  <- project(coords_v, world_crs)
coords_sf_mollweide <- st_as_sf(coords_v_mollweide)  # wingen wants sf/data.frame/matrix, not SpatVector
```
## 2.2 Ocean Layer
```{r 2.2 Ocean Layer}
ocean_map_scale <- 10 # ne_download(scale): The scale of map to return, one of '110', '50', '10' or 'small', 'medium', 'large'.
domain_type <- tolower(Sys.getenv("DOMAIN_TYPE", unset = "ocean"))
if (!domain_type %in% c("ocean", "land")) stop("DOMAIN_TYPE must be ocean or land")
map_type <- domain_type # ne_download(type): type of natural earth file to download one of 'countries', 'map_units', 'map_subunits', 'sovereignty', 'states' OR the portion of any natural earth vector url after the scale and before the . e.g. for 'ne_50m_urban_areas.zip' this would be 'urban_areas'. See Details. OR the raster filename e.g. for 'MSR_50M.zip' this would be 'MSR_50M'
# ocean <- ne_download(type = map_type, category = "physical", scale = ocean_map_scale, returnclass = "sv")
ocean <- ne_get(type = map_type, category = "physical", scale = ocean_map_scale, returnclass = "sv")  # ne_get(): defined in section 1.3, same cache
# Same reasoning as world_land above, but terra's CRS getter can come back
# as either NA or an empty string for "undefined" depending on version, so
# both are checked here.
ocean_crs <- terra::crs(ocean)
if (is.na(ocean_crs) || nchar(ocean_crs) == 0) terra::crs(ocean) <- "EPSG:4326"


# Crop to a generous box around the actual samples before reprojecting
# (avoids reprojecting irrelevant, distant coastline).
bb  <- as.vector(ext(project(coords_v_mollweide, crs(ocean))))
pad <- 10  # degrees
zoom_area <- ext(bb["xmin"] - pad, bb["xmax"] + pad, bb["ymin"] - pad, bb["ymax"] + pad)
ocean <- crop(ocean, zoom_area)
ocean <- project(ocean, world_crs)
```
## 2.3 (coords_to_raster) Building the raster
```{r 2.3 (coords_to_raster) Building the raster}
# resolution_m <- 20 * 1e3            # 20 km; revisit after preview_gd() below
# resolution_m <- 10 * 1e3            # 10 km; revisit after preview_gd() below
# resolution_m <- 5 * 1e3            # 10 km; revisit after preview_gd() below
#resolution_m <- 2.5 * 1e3            # 10 km; revisit after preview_gd() below

# buffer_m needs to stay finite even when MAX_INTERP_DIST doesn't
# (mode = "none") - coords_to_raster() can't extend a raster by an
# infinite margin, and Inf * 1.5 is still Inf. Falls back to the
# window-footprint reach specifically (always finite, since wdim_value/
# fact_value/resolution_m never are) as a sensible minimum margin
# regardless of which masking mode is active - not a flat distance
# regardless of local sample density either way.
buffer_basis_m <- if (is.finite(MAX_INTERP_DIST)) MAX_INTERP_DIST else (window_based_reach_km * 1e3)
buffer_m     <- buffer_basis_m * 1.5  # margin past the eventual display cutoff (section 4),

# coords_to_raster()'s `buffer` argument is in CELLS (it's passed
# straight to terra::extend(), which treats a bare number as rows/
# columns to add per side), not map units - convert once here so the
# rest of the script can keep thinking in meters via buffer_m.
# buffer_cells <- round(buffer_m / resolution_m)
buffer_cells <- ceiling(buffer_m / resolution_m)

#buffer_cells <- 1 #  Ries et al. (2023)

# plot = TRUE gives an immediate sanity check of resolution/extent
# against the sample points, without a separate manual plot() call.
lyr <- coords_to_raster(coords_v_mollweide, buffer = buffer_cells, disagg = ctr_disagg, res = resolution_m, plot = TRUE)
```
## 2.4 Masking the raster using the ocean layer
```{r 2.4 build-raster-ocean-masking}
# mask_gd(), not terra::mask() directly: mask_gd() has no `touches`
# argument, so it always calls terra::mask(x, y) with terra's own
# default, touches = TRUE - a cell survives if it merely overlaps the
# ocean polygon at all. That matters here specifically because `lyr`
# defines window_gd()'s entire working domain (which cells can even be
# considered as window centers), not just how the final map looks.
# The stricter option (touches = FALSE, only reachable via
# terra::mask() directly - a cell survives only if its centre is in
# the ocean polygon) leaves zero valid cells across anything narrower
# than ~resolution_m end-to-end (straits, fjords, many island coasts) -
# a gap the na.rm = TRUE fix in section 3 can't rescue, since there's
# nothing non-NA left in that neighborhood to average over in the
# first place. Section 4 masks kgd/ocean through mask_gd() too, for the
# same reason and the same touches = TRUE treatment - see the comment
# there for the coastline-sharpness trade-off that implies.
lyr <- mask_gd(lyr, ocean)
```
## 2.5 (preview_gd) Raster preview before trusting wdim/fact
```{r 2.5 preview_gd}
# Native preview_gd() draws directly and returns a sample-count SpatRaster,
# not a ggplot for ggsave(). Call twice for inline display and PNG output.
# Window coverage is controlled by wdim/fact; maxdist is for circle/resist
# previews. This parameter-choice aid is independent of efficiency checks
# and can still be expensive on a global raster.
# Inspect sample coverage to choose suitable wdim/fact settings. This preview
# is enabled by default and is independent of efficiency diagnostics.
if (preview_windows) {
  wingen::preview_gd(lyr, coords_sf_mollweide, method = "window",
    wdim = wdim_value, fact = fact_value, sample_count = TRUE, min_n = min_n_samples_per_calc)
  window_preview_output_filename <- paste0(output_prefix, "window_preview_buffer_", buffer_cells, ".png")
  png(file.path(output_dir, window_preview_output_filename), width = 10, height = 6, units = "in", res = 300)
  wingen::preview_gd(lyr, coords_sf_mollweide, method = "window",
    wdim = wdim_value, fact = fact_value, sample_count = TRUE, min_n = min_n_samples_per_calc)
  invisible(dev.off())
}
# Optional grid search when retuning for a new dataset/region:
# for (w in c(3, 5, 7)) {
#   for (f in c(3, 5, 7)) {
#     wingen::preview_gd(lyr, coords_sf_mollweide, method = "window",
#       wdim = w, fact = f, sample_count = TRUE, min_n = min_n_samples_per_calc)
#   }
# }

```
## 2.6 Environmental layers (salinity, temperature, chlorophyll, oxygen, current speed)
CopernicusMarine downloads the products selected by `ENV_PRESET` in
`config/env_presets.yaml`. Physics supplies salinity, temperature and the
eastward/northward current components. Dissolved oxygen comes from the
separate biogeochemical reanalysis; chlorophyll remains the satellite
ocean-colour product. Oxygen and current speed have their own config toggles.

All layers use the selected baseline years. Oxygen is the mean dissolved
oxygen concentration (mmol/m³). Current speed (m/s) is calculated as
`sqrt(uo^2 + vo^2)` for each monthly time step, then averaged across the
baseline. Monthly mean components cannot resolve faster changes in speed
or direction. Calculating the magnitude before the baseline mean avoids
cancellation between months with opposing currents.

This section builds the layers and extracts values at each individual's
coordinates. Section 7 calculates window Pearson correlations at the raw
diversity cell centres, and location Pearson/Spearman associations against
the environmental values averaged over each cluster's member individuals.
The optional neutral comparisons use those same location predictors.

Credentials are never hardcoded here: cms_download_subset() picks them up
automatically from the COPERNICUSMARINE_SERVICE_USERNAME /
COPERNICUSMARINE_SERVICE_PASSWORD environment variables (set once in your
shell profile or the batch script - see cms_set_username()/
cms_set_password() to store them that way from an interactive session).

Note: this section is written and checked against the package's documented
API and source, but not run end-to-end here against the live Copernicus
service (no account/network access in this environment) - the diagnostic
prints below (dimension names, NA counts) are there specifically so the
first real run surfaces a wrong depth/variable-name guess immediately
instead of silently producing a flat or empty layer.
```{r 2.6 Environmental layers}
USE_COPERNICUS_MARINE <- as.logical(Sys.getenv("USE_COPERNICUS_MARINE", unset = "FALSE"))
# USE_COPERNICUS_MARINE <- TRUE
if (USE_COPERNICUS_MARINE) {
  # ---- cache dir: same reasoning as ne_cache_dir above - shared across every
  # gene's render and across chromosomes, since none of this depends on the
  # gene at all (only on the sample coordinates and the config below) ----
  env_cache_dir <- Sys.getenv("ENV_CACHE_DIR", unset = file.path(dirname(output_dir), "env_cache"))
  dir.create(env_cache_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

  # Requested physics depth also applies to currents. Oxygen defaults to
  # the same depth; ENV_OXYGEN_DEPTH_M can select a different layer.
  ENV_DEPTH_M <- as.numeric(Sys.getenv("ENV_DEPTH_M", unset = 0))
  ENV_OXYGEN_DEPTH_M <- as.numeric(Sys.getenv("ENV_OXYGEN_DEPTH_M", unset = as.character(ENV_DEPTH_M)))
  read_environment_toggle <- function(name) {
    value <- tolower(trimws(Sys.getenv(name, unset = "FALSE")))
    if (!(value %in% c("true", "false"))) stop(name, " must be TRUE or FALSE")
    value == "true"
  }
  ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED <- read_environment_toggle("ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED")
  ENV_CURRENT_SPEED_ENABLED <- read_environment_toggle("ENV_CURRENT_SPEED_ENABLED")
  if (!is.finite(ENV_DEPTH_M) || ENV_DEPTH_M < 0 ||
      (ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED && (!is.finite(ENV_OXYGEN_DEPTH_M) || ENV_OXYGEN_DEPTH_M < 0))) {
    stop("Environmental depths must be finite, non-negative metres")
  }

  # Multi-year window the winter/summer/overall means are computed over - several years, not one, so a single
  # unusual year doesn't dominate. Set ENV_BASELINE_START_YEAR / ENV_BASELINE_END_YEAR in config.yaml
  # (wingen_params); each dataset's own coverage limits are applied further down (env_presets.yaml), so a range
  # that reaches past a dataset's end is trimmed instead of failing. The 2019-2022 fallback below was a
  # first-test placeholder to keep the first download small - a longer climatology (10-30 years) is a more
  # defensible proxy for the conditions the species are adapted to.
  # If you change ENV_WINTER_MONTHS / ENV_SUMMER_MONTHS below, use a new results_dir (or delete the cached
  # temp_* files): the cache file names carry product, depth and years, but not the months.
  ENV_BASELINE_START_YEAR <- as.numeric(Sys.getenv("ENV_BASELINE_START_YEAR", unset = 2019))
  ENV_BASELINE_END_YEAR   <- as.numeric(Sys.getenv("ENV_BASELINE_END_YEAR",   unset = 2022))

  # split water temperature into a "winter" and a "summer" metric,
  # winter roughly Nov-Jan (species assumed less active then).
  # Summer will here be defined as Jun-Aug.
  ENV_WINTER_MONTHS <- c(11, 12, 1)
  ENV_SUMMER_MONTHS <- c(6, 7, 8)

  # >>> [env-presets] ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # ---- product/layer choice - the ONE place this is decided ----
  # Choose a preset with ENV_PRESET in config.yaml (wingen_params). The presets themselves - product, layer,
  # variable names, the years each dataset covers, and notes on when to use which - live in
  # config/env_presets.yaml. To use another Copernicus Marine dataset, add an entry there: no edit to this file.
  ENV_PRESET       <- Sys.getenv("ENV_PRESET", unset = "global")
  ENV_PRESETS_FILE <- Sys.getenv("ENV_PRESETS_FILE",
                                 unset = file.path(github_repository_path, "config", "env_presets.yaml"))
  if (!file.exists(ENV_PRESETS_FILE)) stop("Environmental presets file not found: ", ENV_PRESETS_FILE)
  env_presets <- yaml::read_yaml(ENV_PRESETS_FILE)$presets
  if (!(ENV_PRESET %in% names(env_presets))) {
    stop("ENV_PRESET '", ENV_PRESET, "' is not defined in ", ENV_PRESETS_FILE,
         ". Available presets: ", paste(names(env_presets), collapse = ", "))
  }
  env_preset <- env_presets[[ENV_PRESET]]

  ENV_PHYSICS_PRODUCT <- env_preset$physics$product            # salinity + temperature + currents
  ENV_PHYSICS_LAYER   <- env_preset$physics$layer
  ENV_SALINITY_VAR    <- env_preset$physics$salinity_var
  ENV_TEMPERATURE_VAR <- env_preset$physics$temperature_var
  ENV_CHL_PRODUCT     <- env_preset$chl$product                # satellite chlorophyll-a
  ENV_CHL_LAYER       <- env_preset$chl$layer
  ENV_CHL_VARIABLE    <- env_preset$chl$variable
  env_preset_fields <- list(ENV_PHYSICS_PRODUCT, ENV_PHYSICS_LAYER, ENV_SALINITY_VAR, ENV_TEMPERATURE_VAR,
                            ENV_CHL_PRODUCT, ENV_CHL_LAYER, ENV_CHL_VARIABLE)
  if (any(vapply(env_preset_fields, function(x) is.null(x) || !nzchar(x), logical(1)))) {
    stop("Preset '", ENV_PRESET, "' in ", ENV_PRESETS_FILE, " must define physics: product, layer, salinity_var, ",
         "temperature_var and chl: product, layer, variable")
  }
  if (ENV_CURRENT_SPEED_ENABLED) {
    ENV_CURRENT_EASTWARD_VAR <- env_preset$physics$current_eastward_var
    ENV_CURRENT_NORTHWARD_VAR <- env_preset$physics$current_northward_var
    if (any(vapply(list(ENV_CURRENT_EASTWARD_VAR, ENV_CURRENT_NORTHWARD_VAR),
                   function(x) is.null(x) || !nzchar(x), logical(1)))) {
      stop("Preset '", ENV_PRESET, "' must define physics: current_eastward_var and current_northward_var")
    }
  }
  if (ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED) {
    ENV_OXYGEN_PRODUCT <- env_preset$oxygen$product
    ENV_OXYGEN_LAYER <- env_preset$oxygen$layer
    ENV_OXYGEN_VARIABLE <- env_preset$oxygen$variable
    if (any(vapply(list(ENV_OXYGEN_PRODUCT, ENV_OXYGEN_LAYER, ENV_OXYGEN_VARIABLE),
                   function(x) is.null(x) || !nzchar(x), logical(1)))) {
      stop("Preset '", ENV_PRESET, "' must define oxygen: product, layer and variable")
    }
  }
  cat("Environmental data preset:", ENV_PRESET, "-", env_preset$label, "\n")
  cat("(available presets in", basename(ENV_PRESETS_FILE), ":", paste(names(env_presets), collapse = ", "), ")\n")

  # Years actually requested from each dataset: the requested baseline (ENV_BASELINE_START/END_YEAR above),
  # trimmed to the coverage the preset declares for that dataset (first_year / last_year in env_presets.yaml;
  # null = no limit). Trimming is announced, and the years used end up in the cache file names and in the gene's
  # JSON (run_settings), so a catalog always says which years its environmental values are averages over.
  clamp_env_years <- function(first_year, last_year, what) {
    start <- ENV_BASELINE_START_YEAR
    end   <- ENV_BASELINE_END_YEAR
    if (!is.null(first_year)) start <- max(start, first_year)
    if (!is.null(last_year))  end   <- min(end,   last_year)
    if (start > end) {
      stop(what, ": the requested baseline ", ENV_BASELINE_START_YEAR, "-", ENV_BASELINE_END_YEAR,
           " does not overlap this dataset's coverage (", first_year, "-", last_year, ")")
    }
    if (start != ENV_BASELINE_START_YEAR || end != ENV_BASELINE_END_YEAR) {
      message("NOTE (", what, "): requested baseline ", ENV_BASELINE_START_YEAR, "-", ENV_BASELINE_END_YEAR,
              " trimmed to ", start, "-", end, " to fit the dataset's coverage")
    }
    c(start, end)
  }
  env_years_physics <- clamp_env_years(env_preset$physics$first_year, env_preset$physics$last_year, "physics")
  env_years_chl     <- clamp_env_years(env_preset$chl$first_year,     env_preset$chl$last_year,     "chlorophyll")
  if (ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED) {
    env_years_oxygen <- clamp_env_years(env_preset$oxygen$first_year, env_preset$oxygen$last_year, "oxygen")
    cat("Oxygen baseline years:", paste(env_years_oxygen, collapse = "-"), "\n")
  }
  cat("Baseline years used - physics:", paste(env_years_physics, collapse = "-"),
      "| chlorophyll:", paste(env_years_chl, collapse = "-"), "\n")
  # <<< [env-presets] ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  # Cover the later 10%-padded display extent, plus a quarter-degree download
  # margin for boundary grid cells. This requests full Copernicus fields;
  # it does not interpolate environmental data from empirical sample means.
  # cms_download_subset()'s `region` is documented as xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax.
  env_region <- c(max(-180, bb_raw[["xmin"]] - 2*pad_raw_x - .25),
                  max(-90, bb_raw[["ymin"]] - 2*pad_raw_y - .25),
                  min(180, bb_raw[["xmax"]] + 2*pad_raw_x + .25),
                  min(90, bb_raw[["ymax"]] + 2*pad_raw_y + .25))
  env_verticalrange <- c(-ENV_DEPTH_M, -ENV_DEPTH_M)  # package docs: values below the surface must be NEGATIVE

  # Loads a previously-cached layer if one exists at cache_path, otherwise
  # calls `build()` (a zero-arg closure doing the actual download) and
  # writes the result there for every later gene's render to reuse - the
  # "fetch once" behavior, done as a simple on-disk check rather than a new
  # Snakemake rule, so it doesn't require restructuring the DAG right now.
  cached_env_raster <- function(cache_path, build) {
    # A previous smaller request must not satisfy a wider study-region request.
    region_tag <- paste(signif(env_region, 10), collapse = "_")
    cache_path <- sub("\\.tif$", paste0("_bbox_", region_tag, ".tif"), cache_path)
    if (file.exists(cache_path)) return(terra::rast(cache_path))
    r <- build()
    # Write to a temporary name first and rename when finished: file.rename() is atomic within one folder, so a
    # gene rendering at the same moment never opens a half-written cache file. Then read the layer back from disk so
    # EVERY gene works with the same stored values (writeRaster stores 32-bit floats - returning the in-memory
    # 64-bit `r` here would have given the very first gene values that differ from everyone else's in the 7th digit).
    tmp_path <- sub("\\.tif$", paste0(".", Sys.getpid(), ".tmp.tif"), cache_path)
    terra::writeRaster(r, tmp_path, overwrite = TRUE)
    file.rename(tmp_path, cache_path)
    terra::rast(cache_path)
  }

  # The package ignores ... when creating its file, so set the flag in a private
  # copy of its writer. Installed package functions and precision stay unchanged.
  write_env_netcdf4 <- local({
    make_writer <- function(writer) {
      count <- 0L
      use_netcdf4 <- function(x) {
        if (!is.call(x)) return(x)
        if (identical(x[[1]], quote(ncdf4::nc_create))) {
          x$force_v4 <- TRUE
          count <<- count + 1L
        }
        for (i in seq_along(x)) {
          if (!identical(x[[i]], quote(expr = ))) x[[i]] <- use_netcdf4(x[[i]])
        }
        x
      }
      body(writer) <- use_netcdf4(body(writer))
      if (count != 1L) stop("Expected one ncdf4::nc_create call in the Copernicus writer; found ", count)
      writer
    }
    writer <- NULL
    function(raw, file) {
      if (is.null(writer)) writer <<- make_writer(getExportedValue("CopernicusMarine", "cms_write_ncdf"))
      writer(raw, file)
    }
  })

  # Retain monthly time steps so vector components can be combined before
  # temporal averaging. NetCDF preserves the timestamps for alignment.
  download_env_series <- function(product, layer, variable, years, vertical = env_verticalrange) {
    raw <- cms_download_subset(
      product = product, layer = layer, variable = variable,
      region = env_region,
      timerange = c(sprintf("%d-01-01", as.integer(years[1])), sprintf("%d-12-31", as.integer(years[2]))),
      verticalrange = vertical,
      progress = FALSE
    )
    nc_tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".nc")
    write_env_netcdf4(raw, nc_tmp)
    r <- terra::rast(nc_tmp)
    cat(layer, "/", variable, ": downloaded", terra::nlyr(r), "time step(s) - layer names:",
        paste(names(r), collapse = ", "), "\n")
    r
  }
  download_env_climatology <- function(product, layer, variable, months, years, vertical = env_verticalrange) {
    r <- download_env_series(product, layer, variable, years, vertical)
    layer_months <- lubridate::month(terra::time(r))
    r <- terra::mean(r[[layer_months %in% months]], na.rm = TRUE)
    terra::project(r, world_crs)
  }

  env_salinity <- cached_env_raster(
    file.path(env_cache_dir, sprintf("salinity_%s_depth%gm_%d-%d.tif", ENV_PHYSICS_PRODUCT, ENV_DEPTH_M, env_years_physics[1], env_years_physics[2])),
    function() download_env_climatology(
      product = ENV_PHYSICS_PRODUCT, layer = ENV_PHYSICS_LAYER, years = env_years_physics,
      variable = ENV_SALINITY_VAR, months = 1:12  # no seasonal split requested for salinity - averaged over the whole baseline window
    )
  )

  env_temp_winter <- cached_env_raster(
    file.path(env_cache_dir, sprintf("temp_winter_%s_depth%gm_%d-%d.tif", ENV_PHYSICS_PRODUCT, ENV_DEPTH_M, env_years_physics[1], env_years_physics[2])),
    function() download_env_climatology(
      product = ENV_PHYSICS_PRODUCT, layer = ENV_PHYSICS_LAYER, years = env_years_physics,
      variable = ENV_TEMPERATURE_VAR, months = ENV_WINTER_MONTHS
    )
  )

  env_temp_summer <- cached_env_raster(
    file.path(env_cache_dir, sprintf("temp_summer_%s_depth%gm_%d-%d.tif", ENV_PHYSICS_PRODUCT, ENV_DEPTH_M, env_years_physics[1], env_years_physics[2])),
    function() download_env_climatology(
      product = ENV_PHYSICS_PRODUCT, layer = ENV_PHYSICS_LAYER, years = env_years_physics,
      variable = ENV_TEMPERATURE_VAR, months = ENV_SUMMER_MONTHS
    )
  )

  # Chlorophyll: a separate satellite product, surface-only (no depth
  # dimension - verticalrange simply omitted), strongly right-skewed hence
  # the log() before anything downstream ever sees it (see the earlier note
  # on this). variable = "CHL" is confirmed directly against the global
  # product's own catalogue listing (data.marine.copernicus.eu); worth a
  # quick cms_product_details() check anyway if ENV_CHL_PRODUCT is ever
  # switched to something not verified here.
  env_chl_log <- cached_env_raster(
    file.path(env_cache_dir, sprintf("chl_log_%s_%d-%d.tif", ENV_CHL_PRODUCT, env_years_chl[1], env_years_chl[2])),
    function() {
      r <- download_env_climatology(
        product = ENV_CHL_PRODUCT, layer = ENV_CHL_LAYER, years = env_years_chl,
        variable = ENV_CHL_VARIABLE, months = 1:12, vertical = NULL
      )
      log(r)
    }
  )

  if (ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED) {
    env_oxygen <- cached_env_raster(
      file.path(env_cache_dir, sprintf("oxygen_%s_%s_%s_depth%gm_%d-%d.tif",
        ENV_OXYGEN_PRODUCT, ENV_OXYGEN_LAYER, ENV_OXYGEN_VARIABLE, ENV_OXYGEN_DEPTH_M,
        env_years_oxygen[1], env_years_oxygen[2])),
      function() download_env_climatology(
        product = ENV_OXYGEN_PRODUCT, layer = ENV_OXYGEN_LAYER, variable = ENV_OXYGEN_VARIABLE,
        months = 1:12, years = env_years_oxygen,
        vertical = c(-ENV_OXYGEN_DEPTH_M, -ENV_OXYGEN_DEPTH_M)
      )
    )
  }
  if (ENV_CURRENT_SPEED_ENABLED) {
    current_speed_magnitude <- function(eastward, northward) sqrt(eastward^2 + northward^2)
    env_current_speed <- cached_env_raster(
      file.path(env_cache_dir, sprintf("current_speed_monthly_%s_%s_%s_%s_depth%gm_%d-%d.tif",
        ENV_PHYSICS_PRODUCT, ENV_PHYSICS_LAYER, ENV_CURRENT_EASTWARD_VAR, ENV_CURRENT_NORTHWARD_VAR,
        ENV_DEPTH_M, env_years_physics[1], env_years_physics[2])),
      function() {
        eastward <- download_env_series(ENV_PHYSICS_PRODUCT, ENV_PHYSICS_LAYER,
          ENV_CURRENT_EASTWARD_VAR, env_years_physics)
        northward <- download_env_series(ENV_PHYSICS_PRODUCT, ENV_PHYSICS_LAYER,
          ENV_CURRENT_NORTHWARD_VAR, env_years_physics)
        times <- terra::time(eastward)
        if (length(times) != terra::nlyr(eastward) || anyNA(times) || anyDuplicated(times) ||
            !identical(times, terra::time(northward)) ||
            !terra::compareGeom(eastward, northward, stopOnError = FALSE)) {
          stop("Current components must have identical grids and valid, matching monthly timestamps")
        }
        speed <- current_speed_magnitude(eastward, northward)
        terra::project(terra::mean(speed, na.rm = TRUE), world_crs)
      }
    )
  }

  # ---- Coastal NA check ----
  # NOT a GPS-accuracy problem - a sample's own coordinate can be exactly
  # right and still land on a masked cell here, because these products' own
  # land masks are coarser than the real coastline (Baltic archipelagos
  # especially) and the ocean-colour product additionally masks a buffer
  # around any coastline for land-adjacency effects. Whether it actually
  # bites THIS dataset is checked directly below rather than assumed either
  # way.
  # >>> [fill-count] per-individual flag: was this individuals raw environmental cell NA (i.e. will it receive a neighbour-filled
  # value below)? Kept per individual (named by Sample ID) so section 4 can count it per location and write it to the JSON.
  environmental_layers <- list(salinity = env_salinity, temp_winter = env_temp_winter,
    temp_summer = env_temp_summer, chl_log = env_chl_log)
  if (ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED) environmental_layers$oxygen <- env_oxygen
  if (ENV_CURRENT_SPEED_ENABLED) environmental_layers$current_speed <- env_current_speed
  env_raw_na_flags <- lapply(
    environmental_layers,
    function(r) {
      flag <- is.na(terra::extract(r, coords_v_mollweide, ID = FALSE)[[1]])
      names(flag) <- coords_file_df$`Sample ID`
      flag
    }
  )
  env_before_na <- vapply(env_raw_na_flags, sum, numeric(1))  # same named vector as before - printed just below
  # <<< [fill-count]
  cat("Sample points falling on a masked/NA environmental cell, before filling (of", nrow(coords_file_df), "):\n")
  print(env_before_na)

  # na.policy = "only": fills JUST the NA cells, from their non-NA
  # neighbors - real ocean values are never touched (see the earlier note
  # on this). Repeated so a coastal gap wider than one 3x3 pass can reach
  # (e.g. a narrow strait) still gets filled.
  fill_coastal_na <- function(r, passes = 2) {
    for (i in seq_len(passes)) r <- terra::focal(r, w = 3, fun = "mean", na.policy = "only", na.rm = TRUE)
    r
  }
  env_salinity    <- fill_coastal_na(env_salinity)
  env_temp_winter <- fill_coastal_na(env_temp_winter)
  env_temp_summer <- fill_coastal_na(env_temp_summer)
  env_chl_log     <- fill_coastal_na(env_chl_log)
  if (ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED) env_oxygen <- fill_coastal_na(env_oxygen)
  if (ENV_CURRENT_SPEED_ENABLED) env_current_speed <- fill_coastal_na(env_current_speed)

  # Per-individual values, in the SAME order as coords_v_mollweide - the
  # same point set window_gd() itself uses for pi in section 3 - so these
  # plug directly into window_general() with identical wdim/fact/coords/lyr
  # settings in section 7 (Track A) with no reordering needed. Named by
  # Sample ID (coords_v_mollweide's row order is coords_file_df's row order
  # - vect()/project() preserve feature order, confirmed) so Track B
  # (section 7, 4c) can pool the same individuals per cluster that
  # pi_for_cluster() itself pools, by ID rather than by position.
  env_ind_salinity    <- terra::extract(env_salinity,    coords_v_mollweide, ID = FALSE)[[1]]
  env_ind_temp_winter <- terra::extract(env_temp_winter, coords_v_mollweide, ID = FALSE)[[1]]
  env_ind_temp_summer <- terra::extract(env_temp_summer, coords_v_mollweide, ID = FALSE)[[1]]
  env_ind_chl_log     <- terra::extract(env_chl_log,     coords_v_mollweide, ID = FALSE)[[1]]
  names(env_ind_salinity)    <- coords_file_df$`Sample ID`
  names(env_ind_temp_winter) <- coords_file_df$`Sample ID`
  names(env_ind_temp_summer) <- coords_file_df$`Sample ID`
  names(env_ind_chl_log)     <- coords_file_df$`Sample ID`
  if (ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED) {
    env_ind_oxygen <- terra::extract(env_oxygen, coords_v_mollweide, ID = FALSE)[[1]]
    names(env_ind_oxygen) <- coords_file_df$`Sample ID`
  }
  if (ENV_CURRENT_SPEED_ENABLED) {
    env_ind_current_speed <- terra::extract(env_current_speed, coords_v_mollweide, ID = FALSE)[[1]]
    names(env_ind_current_speed) <- coords_file_df$`Sample ID`
  }

  # >>> [fill-count] individuals that still have NO environmental value after filling (they drop out of their location's mean)
  env_after_na <- c(salinity    = sum(is.na(env_ind_salinity)),
                    temp_winter = sum(is.na(env_ind_temp_winter)),
                    temp_summer = sum(is.na(env_ind_temp_summer)),
                    chl_log     = sum(is.na(env_ind_chl_log)))
  if (ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED) env_after_na <- c(env_after_na, oxygen = sum(is.na(env_ind_oxygen)))
  if (ENV_CURRENT_SPEED_ENABLED) env_after_na <- c(env_after_na, current_speed = sum(is.na(env_ind_current_speed)))
  cat("individuals with NO environmental value even after filling:\n")
  print(env_after_na)
  # <<< [fill-count]
  }
```
# 3. Moving-window genetic diversity (window_gd / window_general)
```{r 3. window-gd}
start_window_gd_time <- Sys.time()
# window_gd(..., fact = fact_value) would rebuild its own working grid internally via terra::aggregate(lyr, fact, fun = mean), without na.rm = TRUE.
# Since lyr is sea = 1 / land = NA, that means an aggregated cell only survives as non-NA if ALL of its resolution_m sub-cells are sea; a single land sub-cell nulls the whole block, and any cell whose own aggregated value is NA is skipped entirely (sample_count = NA, no window ever evaluated), regardless of real samples sitting right there.
# By aggregating with na.rm = TRUE first, then passing fact = 0 so window_gd() doesn't re-aggregate, keeps the same window geometry while fixing which cells are eligible to be evaluated at all.

lyr_agg <- terra::aggregate(lyr, fact = fact_value, fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE)
# Select native functions or tested efficient adapters using the TOTAL
# aggregated working-grid cell count (masked cells included): >= threshold
# selects efficient mode; 0 selects it for any grid, Inf selects native.
# The raster extent, resolution, origin and empirical coordinates stay the
# same. Windows evaluate only eligible focal cells, pooling the same member
# individuals and preserving the native estimator and rarefaction RNG order.
# Kriging keeps native observations, variogram/model fitting, weights and
# neighborhood settings, but predicts domain cells in bounded batches.
# This changes the worklist, not the grd geometry passed to the function.
# Version/argument compatibility checks can fall back to native execution.
# These are local bindings; wingen:: functions themselves remain untouched.
wingen_functions <- wingen_helpers$configure_wingen(lyr_agg, ocean,
  min_cells = grid_min_cells, chunk_cells = kriging_chunk_cells, diagnostics = diagnostic_run)
window_gd <- wingen_functions$window_gd
window_general <- wingen_functions$window_general
wkrig_gd <- wingen_functions$wkrig_gd
grid_efficiency <- attr(wingen_functions, "optimized")
# lyr = lyr_agg with fact = 0 is required together, and must NOT be changed independently, since window_gd(fact = 0) stops window_gd() from redoing the aggregation made in lyr_agg.
# window_gd(fact) would otherwise rebuild its own working grid internally via terra::aggregate(lyr, fact, fun = mean), WITHOUT na.rm = TRUE.
# Since lyr is sea = (1 / land) = NA, an aggregated cell would then only survive as non-NA if ALL of its fact_value^2 sub-cells are sea
#    => a single land sub-cell nulls the whole block, silently dropping coastal samples from ever getting a window evaluated, regardless of resolution_m (finer resolution => more sub-cells per block
#    => MORE chances one clips land, not fewer).

# Wingen subsets x with x[sub, ] and drops dimensions for one individual.
# Requiring at least two prevents a many-marker row being mistaken for a one-marker column by the custom dosage callback. The normal default is 2.
if (gd_uses_general && (min_n_samples_per_calc < 2L || (use_rarify && rarify_n < 2L))) {
  stop("D/theta windows require MIN_N_SAMPLES_PER_CALC >= 2 and, when rarefying, RARIFY_N >= 2")
}

set.seed(seed_value) # rarefaction inside window_gd() draws random individuals; a fixed seed (SEED in config.yaml) makes every re-run give the same window values

# gd_uses_general <- TRUE
if (gd_uses_general) {
  # The implemented custom hierfstat statistics of tajimas_d (hierfstat::TajimaD.dosage) and theta (hierfstat::theta.Watt.dosage) uses a custom callback, so converting to individuals x markers is done explicitly.
  # Unlike the window_gd branch, this creates dosage_matrix in our environment, which can be reused by the later location calculations.
  dosage_matrix <- gd_input_from_vcf(vcf, gd_stat)
  if (!identical(as.character(coords_file_df$`Sample ID`), rownames(dosage_matrix)) ||
      nrow(dosage_matrix) != nrow(coords_sf_mollweide)) {
    stop("Dosage rows and coordinate rows must have identical individual order")
  }
  wgd <- window_general(
    x = dosage_matrix,
    coords = coords_sf_mollweide,
    lyr = lyr_agg,
    stat = gd_window_fun,
    wdim = wdim_value, # [Default: 3x3 window]
    fact = 0, # must stay 0 (see comment above) [Default: 0]
    rarify = use_rarify,
    rarify_n = rarify_n, # rarify_n: If rarify = TRUE, number of points to use for rarefaction (defaults to min_n). [Default: 2]
    rarify_nit	= rarify_n_iterations, # If rarify = TRUE, number of iterations to use for rarefaction (defaults to 5). Can also be set to "all" to use all possible combinations of samples of size rarify_n within the window. [Default: 5]
    min_n = min_n_samples_per_calc
    # fun is omitted: Wingen defaults to mean and averages rarefaction draws with na.rm=TRUE, exactly as in window_gd(). No metric-specific override.
    # L/rarify_alleles/sig are for Wingen's built-in estimators; the custom callback handles theta's L itself, and tajimas_d has no L argument.
  )
} else {
  wgd <- window_gd(vcf,
                 coords = coords_sf_mollweide,
                 lyr = lyr_agg,
                 stat = gd_stat, # "pi", "Ho" or "biallelic_richness" 
                 wdim = wdim_value, # [Default: 3x3 window]
                 fact = 0, # must stay 0 (see comment above) [Default: 0]
                 rarify = use_rarify,
                 rarify_n = rarify_n, # rarify_n: If rarify = TRUE, number of points to use for rarefaction (defaults to min_n). [Default: 2]
                 rarify_nit	= rarify_n_iterations, # If rarify = TRUE, number of iterations to use for rarefaction (defaults to 5). Can also be set to "all" to use all possible combinations of samples of size rarify_n within the window. [Default: 5]
                 min_n = min_n_samples_per_calc,
                 L = "nvariants" # For calculating "pi", L argument in pi.dosage function. "nvariants" counts SNP columns (not true surveyed sequence length) so this is "diversity per polymorphic site" rather than a properly bp-scaled per-nucleotide pi -> Should ideally be replaced with a true sequence length value for L. [Default: "nvariants"]
                 # L = 100 # For calculating "pi", L argument in pi.dosage function. Return the average nucleotide diversity per nucleotide given the length L of the sequence. The wingen default is L = "nvariants", which sets L to the number of variants in the VCF. If L = NULL, returns the sum over SNPs of nucleotide diversity (note: L = NULL is the pi.dosage default which wingen does not use). [Default: "nvariants"]

                 )
}



names(wgd)

# Name of the chosen statistic's layer in wgd. Everything below looks it up through this variable, never through a hardcoded pi layer name.
gd_layer_name <- setdiff(names(wgd), "sample_count")

# Entirely undefined custom statistics can leave only sample_count in Wingen's result. A heatmap is required, so stop here rather than insert an empty layer or continue into location/neutral summaries without usable moving windows.
if (length(gd_layer_name) != 1L || !any(is.finite(terra::values(wgd[[gd_layer_name]])))) {
  stop("No defined ", gd_label, " moving windows were produced; heatmap computation cannot continue")
}

# wgd <- window_gd(vcf,
#                  coords = coords_sf_mollweide,
#                  #lyr = lyr_agg,
#                  lyr = lyr,
#                  stat = "pi",
#                  wdim = wdim_value, # [Default: 3x3 window]
#                 # fact = 0, # [Default: 0]
#                  fact = fact_value, # [Default: 0]
#                  rarify = TRUE,
#                  rarify_n = 4, # rarify_n: If rarify = TRUE, number of points to use for rarefaction (defaults to min_n). [Default: 2]
#                  rarify_nit	= 5, # If rarify = TRUE, number of iterations to use for rarefaction (defaults to 5). Can also be set to "all" to use all possible combinations of samples of size rarify_n within the window. [Default: 5]
#                  L = "nvariants"
#                # L = 100 # For calculating "pi", L argument in pi.dosage function. Return the average nucleotide diversity per nucleotide given the length L of the sequence. The wingen default is L = "nvariants", which sets L to the number of variants in the VCF. If L = NULL, returns the sum over SNPs of nucleotide diversity (note: L = NULL is the pi.dosage default which wingen does not use). [Default: "nvariants"]
#                  )

window_gd_runtime <- difftime(Sys.time(), start_window_gd_time , units = "secs")
message("window_gd runtime: ", round(window_gd_runtime, 2), " seconds")
print(paste0("window_gd runtime: ", round(window_gd_runtime, 2), " seconds"))
```
## Sample-count diagnostic
Decides minval_sample_count below from real numbers instead of a guess -
what does wgd actually see near EACH real point? Sorted ascending:
whatever minval_sample_count gets set to next, every row above that value
is a real, named sample this pipeline would drop from both the kriging
input and the final display. Worth re-running any time wdim_value/
fact_value/resolution_m/the ROI change.
```{r sample-count-diagnostic}
sample_count_at_point <- terra::extract(wgd[["sample_count"]], coords_v_mollweide)$sample_count
# order(), not sort(), for both lines below: sort() drops NA values by
# default, order() keeps every position and just decides where NAs go -
# using sort() separately from order() is what caused the crash (a
# 122-length vector next to 125 reordered rows, three real samples with
# sample_count_at_point = NA silently dropped by sort()). na.last =
# FALSE additionally puts any NA cases FIRST rather than last - a
# sample with no registered window at all is a worse case than any
# numeric count, and default sorting would otherwise bury it past where
# head(20) below ever looks.
ord <- order(sample_count_at_point, na.last = FALSE)
support_check <- coords_file_df[ord, c("Sample ID", "Latitude", "Longitude")]
support_check$sample_count_at_point <- sample_count_at_point[ord]
head(support_check, 20)
```
#4. (wkrig_gd) Kriging
```{r 4. Kriging (wkrig_gd)}
# --- knob 1: minimum real samples backing a cell. Used here to protect
# the variogram fit itself, not just to hide weak cells from the final
# display afterward - the fitted model describes "how does pi
# similarity decay with distance" using every non-NA cell in wgd as
# input, all at once, regardless of how much real sample support any
# individual cell actually had. A handful of noisy, low-confidence
# windows sitting alongside confident ones can distort that single
# global fit even for predictions made in well-supported areas, since
# the same model gets applied everywhere. Filtering them out before
# kriging protects the model; the mask_gd() masking further below still
# protects the DISPLAYED output afterward - the two aren't redundant
# with each other; the diagnostic chunk above is what should actually
# set this number, not a guess.
#
# 2, not a stricter number: window_gd()'s own min_n (default 2) already
# refuses to compute pi at all below that - anything higher than 2 here
# is a SECOND, stricter cut on top of that decision. Start at 2 (i.e.
# trust window_gd()'s own judgment and no further) and only raise it if
# the diagnostic above and the variogram fit both look better for it.


wgd_confident <- wgd
wgd_confident[[gd_layer_name]] <- mask_gd(wgd[[gd_layer_name]], wgd[["sample_count"]], minval = minval_sample_count)

if (!any(is.finite(terra::values(wgd_confident[[gd_layer_name]])))) {
  stop("No defined ", gd_label, " windows remain after the sample-count mask; kriging cannot continue")
}

# nmax caps how many neighboring points can inform a single prediction -
# unrelated to what gets interpolated (r's job, below) or where (grd's
# job, below). Lower limits can reduce computation but can also change
# predictions; fewer neighbours do not guarantee a smoother surface.
#
# r = wgd_confident[[gd_layer_name]], not the whole wgd_confident object: if r
# has more than one layer, wkrig_gd() silently keeps only the FIRST one
# ("Input raster has multiple layers. Using only the first layer.") -
# wgd_confident is (pi, sample_count) in that order, so passing the
# whole object happens to still krige pi, but only by layer position,
# not by name. Being explicit here means that stays true even if a
# future edit changes what layers wgd_confident carries or their order.
#
# grd = lyr, not disagg(wgd, ...): grd is ONLY a coordinate template -
# "predict at every (x, y) in this grid's geometry" - its own cell
# values are never read (unlike r, grd is extracted with na.rm = FALSE,
# so even its NA cells get a prediction). grd = lyr means predicting
# everywhere in lyr's footprint, including land, which is exactly why
# the separate land re-mask right below is necessary, not optional. It
# also keeps kgd on the exact same grid as lyr/ocean, which the
# sample_count mask further below relies on.

start_wkrig_gd_time <- Sys.time()
# Disaggregating the prediction grid (smoothing) prior to kriging: same geometry as lyr, just subdivided into sub-cells with finer spacing  for wkrig_gd() to report predictions at (see grd_disagg_factor comment in settings above).
# The older kriging function, krig_gd() had an argument for this (disagg_grd), which have not been transferred over to the new kriging function, hence, terra:s disagg function is used here to create a finer grid instead!
grd_fine <- if (grd_disagg_factor > 1) terra::disagg(lyr, fact = grd_disagg_factor) else lyr

if (use_weighted_kriging) {
# weight_r test:
kgd <- wkrig_gd(r = wgd_confident[[gd_layer_name]],
                grd = grd_fine,
                weight_r = wgd_confident[["sample_count"]], # weight_r: Optional SpatRaster with sample counts per cell, used to compute location-specific measurement variance and weights for kriging. If NULL (default), no weighting is applied. [Default: NULL]
                  nmax = nmax_neighbours,
                  maxdist = maxdist,
                  max_range_frac = max_range_frac
                )
} else {
  # Pre 2026-08-25 kriging settings:
  kgd <- wkrig_gd(r = wgd_confident[[gd_layer_name]],
                  grd = grd_fine,
                  nmax = nmax_neighbours,
                  maxdist = maxdist,
                  max_range_frac = max_range_frac
                  )
  
}
# Neighborhood settings can also produce only NA predictions without an error.
# Require an actual kriged surface before proceeding to plots/location summaries.
if (!any(is.finite(terra::values(kgd)))) {
  stop("Kriging produced no defined ", gd_label, " predictions; heatmap computation cannot continue")
}


wkrig_gd_runtime <- difftime(Sys.time(), start_wkrig_gd_time , units = "secs")
message("wkrig_gd runtime: ", round(wkrig_gd_runtime, 2), " seconds")
print(paste0("wkrig_gd runtime: ", round(wkrig_gd_runtime, 2), " seconds"))

# Re-exclude land explicitly. wkrig_gd() interpolates onto whatever
# prediction grid it builds internally and can smooth land back in even
# though `lyr` already had it as NA going in.
# mask_gd()'s implicit touches = TRUE here means the coastline in the
# final figure can bleed very slightly onto land wherever a cell merely
# touches the sea, in exchange for not re-losing the same narrow-water
# sites this exact mechanism was excluding earlier in the pipeline
# (section 2.3). A sharper, centre-based edge is only reachable via
# terra::mask(kgd, ocean, touches = FALSE) directly, at that cost.
mgd <- mask_gd(kgd, ocean)
```
# 5. Masking 

## 5.1 Polygon masking
```{r 5.1 Polygon masking}
if (!is.na(masking_polygon_file_path)) {
  mask_lyr <- rast(masking_polygon_file_path)  # rast(), not terra:::rast() - a normal exported
                                                 # function, no reason to reach into terra's
                                                 # internal namespace for it

  # Diagnostic, not decoration: mask_lyr is coming from an external source
  # (HELCOM/HOLAS in this case) with no guarantee of matching mgd's CRS,
  # resolution, or value encoding. Worth actually looking at before trusting
  # the mask below.
  cat("Species range file CRS:\n"); print(crs(mask_lyr, describe = TRUE))
  cat("Species range file native grid:\n"); print(mask_lyr)
  cat("Distinct values present:", paste(unique(na.omit(values(mask_lyr))), collapse = ", "), "\n")

  # mask_lyr is virtually certain to NOT already be on mgd's own grid (this
  # pipeline's bespoke +proj=moll +lon_0=0 at whatever resolution_m/
  # grd_disagg_factor produced) - that CRS/geometry mismatch is exactly
  # what "[mask] extents do not match" means: terra::mask() requires x and y
  # to share the same grid when y is a SpatRaster, not just an overlapping
  # area. project(source, target_raster, method) reprojects AND resamples
  # onto target_raster's exact geometry in one step - same pattern already
  # used for dist_to_sample in section 5.
  # method = "near": this is a categorical presence/range layer, not a
  # continuous one - averaging class codes across cells (the default
  # "bilinear") would produce meaningless intermediate values.
  mask_lyr_aligned <- project(mask_lyr, mgd, method = "near")

  # mask_gd()/terra::mask() masks wherever y is NA by default - correct
  # if absence is coded as NA in this file, but silently a no-op if this
  # file instead uses an explicit 0 (or other value) for absence with no
  # NA at all. Check the distinct-values print above; if presence isn't
  # bare 1-vs-NA, replace the line below with something explicit instead,
  # e.g.: mask_lyr_aligned[mask_lyr_aligned != 1] <- NA
  mgd_polygon <- mask_gd(mgd, mask_lyr_aligned)

  ggplot_gd(mgd_polygon) + ggtitle(paste0(gd_label, ", species-range-masked"))
}

```

## 5.2 Automatic Masking
### 5.2.1 Sample Count Mask
```{r 5.2.1 Sample Count Mask - automatic-mask}
# minval_sample_count now defined above, reused here for the final display
# mask. sample_count is resampled (nearest-neighbor - it's a count, not
# something to interpolate) straight onto mgd's own grid, rather than
# disagg()'d from wgd by a fixed factor: mgd is on lyr's grid (the
# krige chunk above krigs onto grd = lyr), and wgd's own grid (the
# fact_value-aggregated one) has no guaranteed relationship to that
# grid's exact resolution/extent. Tying this to mgd's actual grid,
# whatever it is, means it can't drift out of sync with mgd if fact_value
# or resolution_m ever change independently of each other.
sample_count <- resample(wgd[["sample_count"]], mgd, method = "near")


# HOTFIX 2026-09-01 (Make better permanent fix in future): When a non-one MAX_INTERP_DIST_SCALE increases the range of interpolated data points to be included, the geometry of the sample count layer still bottleneck the size of the interpolated "clusters". Hence to ensure that the size of these clusters is not limited by the sample count layer, as well as to ensure that the shape of the clusters wont take on the sample count layers rectangular shape, an easy fix to this was just to ensure that no sample count layer-based masking is made.
# The cons with this approach however is that there is no sample count based masking of empirical + interpolated data point existing now for this specific case when you have set MAX_INTERP_DIST_SCALE > 1
if ( (MIN_SAMPLE_COUNT_MODE != "none") && (MAX_INTERP_DIST_SCALE == 1) ) {
      mgd_honest   <- mask_gd(mgd, sample_count, minval = minval_sample_count)
}else { # If either sample count mode has been set to none OR MAX_INTERP_DIST_SCALE has been set to value larger than 1, masking is skipped.
      mgd_honest <- mgd # Sample Count Masking Skipped
 }


```
### 5.2.2 Distance Mask (from nearest empirical data point)
Maximum distance from a cell to the nearest real sample
```{r 5.2.2-Distance Mask - automatic-mask}
start_distance_masking_time <- Sys.time()
# MAX_INTERP_DIST was already decided in section 1.4 (window-based reach by
# default, or the SPACING_CLUSTER_KM-based clustered figure, or a direct
# MAX_INTERP_DIST_KM override) - not redone here, so this and buffer_m
# (section 2.3) both tie back to the exact same number rather than being
# picked independently. This is also where planar-vs-geodesic distance
# matters: terra computes true geodesic distance for a geographic CRS and
# only planar distance for a projected one (like the Mollweide coordinates
# used everywhere else in this script), and that gap is real at this data's
# scale (measured ~10-15% at the few-km-to-tens-of-km range that matters
# here) - which is why the vector/raster below are built in plain WGS84
# specifically for this calculation, rather than folding maxdist into
# wkrig_gd() directly on the Mollweide-projected grid.

# Built directly in WGS84, rather than by reprojecting individual
# Mollweide cell centers back to WGS84. Some cell centers, near the
# edges of a Mollweide extent this wide, can fall outside Mollweide's
# own valid elliptical domain and fail to reproject; reprojecting INTO
# Mollweide from WGS84 (forward direction, below) doesn't have this
# failure mode - every valid lon/lat has a defined Mollweide position,
# it's only the reverse direction that can fail.
wgs84_bb <- st_bbox(coords_raw_sf)  # real lon/lat extent of all samples, from section 1.3

# WGS84_DIST_PAD must be generous enough that wgs84_grid's extent fully
# covers mgd_honest's own extent (bb_raw + buffer_m) once reprojected - a
# too-narrow pad here previously let a real bug through: cells in
# mgd_honest that fall OUTSIDE wgs84_grid's extent get NA from project()
# below (nothing there to sample), and with the OLD too_far <- dist >
# MAX_INTERP_DIST; mask(x, too_far, maskvalues = TRUE) pattern, NA >
# MAX_INTERP_DIST evaluates to NA, not TRUE - terra::mask() with an
# explicit maskvalues only matches THAT value, it does not also treat NA
# as "mask this" the way its own default behavior would. So those cells
# silently passed the "too far" check no matter how far away they
# actually were (confirmed via the spot-check above, near Iceland, where
# no real sample exists). mask_gd() below sidesteps this differently: it
# has no maskvalues argument at all, it always calls plain terra::mask(x,
# y) - which DOES mask wherever y is NA, by default. So an unknown
# distance is already treated as "not confirmed close enough" without
# needing a separate manual failsafe line.
#
# Tied to buffer_m (doubled, for margin) rather than a flat number: a flat
# 20-degree pad made sense for the original globally-dispersed dataset,
# but is far more than buffer_m actually needs at this dataset's scale -
# and that starts to matter once resolution is tightened below, since
# cell count scales with pad^2. An oversized pad and a fine resolution
# together would have made this genuinely slow for no accuracy benefit.
WGS84_DIST_PAD <- (buffer_m / 111320) * 2  # metres -> degrees (~111.32 km/degree), doubled for margin

# WGS84_DIST_PAD above assumes 111.32 km/degree, which is only accurate for LATITUDE
# (a degree of LONGITUDE covers cos(latitude) times less real distance)
# For stockholm region for instance (~59 latitude) that's roughly half (cos(59) =~ 0.51).
# If the same distance pad would therefore be applied to both directions it would lead to under-covers for east-west specifically: wgs84_grid's real reach in that direction is only ~half what the pad number implies, so its edge sits closer to the samples than intended).
# Cells in mgd_honest beyond THAT (too-close) edge get NA from the project() call below and mask_gd() would then masks them out regardless of true distance. 
WGS84_DIST_PAD_LON <- WGS84_DIST_PAD / cos(mean(wgs84_bb[c("ymin", "ymax")]) * pi / 180)

# Also tied to resolution_m rather than a flat number: at the old 0.5-deg
# (~55 km) resolution, MAX_INTERP_DIST (now ~4.6-26 km, i.e. SMALLER than
# one grid cell) couldn't actually be resolved - every mgd_honest cell
# reprojecting near-neighbor onto the same 55 km wgs84_grid cell got the
# identical distance value regardless of real differences in how close
# each one truly is to a sample. This was already too coarse before
# today, just not by enough to be obvious until MAX_INTERP_DIST itself
# got fixed to a realistic (small) number.

# To ensure that mgd_honest "lives on" a resolution_m grid (mgd_honest's real cell size is resolution_m / grd_disagg_factor, since grd_fine (used to build kgd/mgd/mgd_honest) disaggregates lyr by grd_disagg_factor first).
# If wgs84_res would be left at plain resolution_m, wgs84_grid would roughly be "grd_disagg_factor" times coarser than what it's being reprojected onto in dist_to_sample below.
# Otherwise the nearest-neighbor reprojection of a coarse WGS84 grid onto a much finer, differently-oriented Mollweide grid would produce a a rotation/reprojection artifact with jagged staircase-like edges on mgd_honest.
# Matching wgs84_res to mgd_honest's actual resolution (This increases wgs84_grid's cell count by roughly grd_disagg_factor^2, so distance() below gets correspondingly slower)
# Also folds in ctr_disagg (currently NULL/inactive - see raster creation parameters above):
# if ctr_disagg is set, lyr's real resolution will be changed in the same way as grd_disagg_factor & and would silently reopen this exact mismatch
lyr_res_m <- resolution_m / (if (!is.null(ctr_disagg)) ctr_disagg else 1)  # lyr's actual cell size, accounting for ctr_disagg
wgs84_res <- (lyr_res_m / grd_disagg_factor) / 111320  # metres -> degrees latitude, matched to mgd_honest's actual (disaggregated) resolution

wgs84_grid <- rast(ext(wgs84_bb["xmin"] - WGS84_DIST_PAD_LON, wgs84_bb["xmax"] + WGS84_DIST_PAD_LON,
    wgs84_bb["ymin"] - WGS84_DIST_PAD, wgs84_bb["ymax"] + WGS84_DIST_PAD),
resolution = wgs84_res, crs = "EPSG:4326")

# Distance to the nearest unique empirical sampling coordinate.
# Repeated coordinates cannot change the minimum; cluster centroids are
# never substituted here, even when they set the optional scalar cutoff.
dist_wgs84 <- distance(wgs84_grid, sample_sites_wgs84)
# The global geographic AOI guides GDAL transformation selection, avoiding
# invalid outer corners of a wide rectangular Mollweide template. It is
# not a crop or a new projection: mgd_honest still defines the output grid.
# The same WGS84/Mollweide operation works for regional/southern datasets;
# this option does not fix separate antimeridian or polar-extent issues.
dist_to_sample <- project(dist_wgs84, mgd_honest, method = "near",
  transOpts = "AREA_OF_INTEREST=-180,-90,180,90")

# Not redundant with wkrig_gd()'s maxdist (see settings block near the
# top): this masks by distance to the nearest actual sample coordinate;
# maxdist there only ever sees wgd_confident[[gd_layer_name]]'s cell centroids.
# With MAX_INTERP_DIST_MODE="none", MAX_INTERP_DIST=Inf and this distance
# mask is disabled. Other domain, count or polygon masks still apply.

mgd_honest <- mask_gd(mgd_honest, dist_to_sample, maxval = MAX_INTERP_DIST)

distance_masking_runtime <- difftime(Sys.time(), start_distance_masking_time , units = "secs")
message("distance masking runtime: ", round(distance_masking_runtime, 2), " seconds")
print(paste0("distance masking runtime: ", round(distance_masking_runtime, 2), " seconds"))
```

   print(quantile(v, c(0, .01, .5, .99, .999, 1), na.rm = TRUE))
   cat("cells > 0.16:", sum(v > 0.16, na.rm = TRUE), "of", sum(is.finite(v)), "\n")
   i <- which.max(v)

   cat("raw max window:", w[j], "| sample_count there:", terra::values(wgd[["sample_count"]])[j, 1], "\n")
