# 6. Plots
## 6.0 Defining plot_with_context (Plot Function)
```{r}
plot_with_context <- function(r, title, legend_name = "value", palette = HEATMAP_COLOR_PALETTE, show_points = FALSE, spherical_grid = SPHERICAL_GRID) {
  r_wgs84 <- project(r, display_template, method = "near")  # nearest-neighbor: avoid
                                                         # smoothing anything beyond
                                                         # what kriging already did
  df <- as.data.frame(r_wgs84, xy = TRUE)
  names(df)[3] <- "value"

  # Reprojecting the FULL global world_land_wgs84 is the likely root cause
  # of the previous attempt's wrong extent: most of a whole-world land
  # layer sits well outside a small regional projection's valid domain,
  # and reprojecting far-outside-domain geometry can produce degenerate
  # output that throws off coord_sf()'s automatic bounding-box calculation.
  # Cropping to a generous regional box first, mirroring how `ocean` is
  # already cropped before reprojection in section 2.2, keeps every point
  # handed to the projection safely within range - only actually needed
  # for the spherical case, since plain WGS84 display has no domain limits
  # to worry about.
  land_for_plot <- if (spherical_grid) {
    crop_box <- sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = display_xlim[1] - 1, xmax = display_xlim[2] + 1,
                              ymin = display_ylim[1] - 1, ymax = display_ylim[2] + 1),
                            crs = sf::st_crs(4326))                             
    suppressWarnings(sf::st_crop(world_land_wgs84, crop_box))
  } else {
    world_land_wgs84
  }

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = land_for_plot, fill = "grey85", color = "grey60", linewidth = 0.2) +
    # geom_tile(), not geom_raster(): the reprojected grid isn't
    # perfectly regular (Mollweide's own distortion, worse toward the
    # edges), and geom_raster() forcibly shifts pixels to fit a regular
    # grid when it isn't - real positional error, not a cosmetic
    # warning. geom_tile() doesn't make that assumption.
    #
    # width/height set explicitly to display_res_deg, not left for
    # geom_tile() to infer from the data: its default resolution() guess
    # (smallest gap between observed x/y values) draws every tile at
    # exactly that size with zero overlap, so whatever pixel grid the
    # current graphics device happens to rasterize into can round two
    # adjacent tiles a hair apart and leave a 1px background seam - this
    # is why the same plot object showed lines in different positions in
    # RStudio's viewer vs. the file ggsave() wrote, since each renders to
    # a different output pixel count. A deliberate 2% oversize forces
    # tiles to overlap instead of merely touch, so no rounding choice by
    # any device can open a gap between them.
    geom_tile(data = df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = value),
              width = display_res_deg * 1.02, height = display_res_deg * 1.02) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = palette, na.value = NA, name = legend_name)

  if (show_points) {
    size_legend_name <- if (SAMPLE_POINT_SIZE_BY == "value") {
      paste("empirical", if (point_values_use_abs) paste0("|", gd_label_short, "|") else gd_label_short)
    } else "n samples"
    p <- p +
      geom_point(data = sample_point_counts,
                 aes(x = Longitude, y = Latitude, size = size_value),
                 shape = 21, fill = "white", color = "black", alpha = 0.5, stroke = 0.3)
    if (SAMPLE_POINT_SIZE_BY == "value" && (point_values_use_abs || gd_stat == "tajimas_d")) {
      # Keep zero-valued points visible for D or metrics sized by magnitude.
      p <- p + scale_size(range = c(1, 6), name = size_legend_name)
    } else {
      # Nonnegative metrics/counts: a value of zero has zero point area.
      p <- p + scale_size_area(max_size = 6, name = size_legend_name)
    }
  }
  
  # Lambert Azimuthal Equal-Area, not orthographic: still curves the
  # graticule (the lat/long grid lines), visually emphasizing that this is
  # a 2D projection of a 3D surface, but with no hard visibility cutoff at
  # 90 degrees from center the way orthographic has - avoiding the domain
  # problem above entirely, rather than just working around it - and a
  # closer visual match to the subtle curvature in the eelgrass Skagerrak-
  # Kattegat reference figure (DOI 10.1111/eva.12914) this feature was
  # originally requested from, which is nothing like orthographic's
  # dramatic "view from space" look. Purely a display choice either way -
  # r itself is untouched, only how coord_sf() renders it changes.
  # Centered on the data's own midpoint rather than an arbitrary default
  # like (0,0), so the curve is naturally centered on the study area.
  if (spherical_grid) {
    spherical_crs <- sprintf("+proj=laea +lat_0=%f +lon_0=%f",
                              mean(display_ylim), mean(display_xlim))

    # xlim/ylim given in plain WGS84 degrees (matching default_crs below),
    # NOT pre-reprojected into spherical_crs's own units - that was the
    # actual bug behind both the too-wide zoom and the wall of "laea:
    # Invalid latitude" warnings. With default_crs set, coord_sf() expects
    # xlim/ylim in default_crs's units and reprojects them itself
    # internally; handing it already-reprojected meter values on top of
    # that double-transformed them, which is exactly what its own request
    # to reproject "x or y limits" was failing on. lims_method =
    # "geometry_bbox" is the fix the warning itself suggested - it avoids
    # the boundary-densification step (sampling extra points along the
    # box's edges to trace the curve accurately) that was generating
    # invalid latitudes in the first place, at the cost of a less
    # precisely-curved edge to the cropped view - not a concern here,
    # since only the four corners matter for a simple rectangular crop.
    p <- p + coord_sf(crs = spherical_crs, default_crs = sf::st_crs(4326),
                       xlim = display_xlim, ylim = display_ylim,
                       lims_method = "geometry_bbox")
  } else {
    p <- p + coord_sf(xlim = display_xlim, ylim = display_ylim, expand = FALSE)
  }
  

  p +
    ggtitle(title) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "aliceblue", color = NA),
          axis.title = element_blank())
}

```

## 6.2 Genetic Diversity Layer Plots (masked ("honest") and unmasked ("sloppy"), for comparison)
"Unmasked" here still respects the land re-mask above (mgd) - for a
marine dataset, interpolated values on land are never wanted. Both a
masked and an unmasked version are kept so either the automatic default
or a fuller view can be pulled depending on who's using the pipeline
and why.

The computation above (window_gd, kriging, both masks) happens under
the Mollweide projection, since this standardizes real-world distance
and ensures equal-area cells. The output rasters are reprojected back
to WGS84 (latitude, longitude) only for display.
```{r 6.2 Genetic Diversity Layer Plots}
start_plotting_time <- Sys.time()

world_land_wgs84 <- world_land  # already sf, EPSG:4326, from section 1.3

# Temp for ries et al:
if (MAX_INTERP_DIST_MODE == "none" && MIN_SAMPLE_COUNT_MODE == "none" && exists("mgd_polygon")) {
  mgd_honest <- mgd_polygon
}

# Empirical area check, for tuning MAX_INTERP_DIST_SCALE against an
# actual target area increase (rather than trusting the sqrt(1+X) formula above):
# run once at MAX_INTERP_DIST_SCALE = 1, note this number -> run again at a candidate scale, compare the ratio against what you actually wanted.
# Needs checking per run rather than computed once, since how much the visible area grows with radius depends on how much neighboring sample points' buffers already overlap at the current scale.
visible_cells <- sum(!is.na(terra::values(mgd_honest)))
visible_area_km2 <- visible_cells * prod(terra::res(mgd_honest)) / 1e6
cat("mgd_honest visible area:", round(visible_area_km2, 1), "km^2 across", visible_cells, "cells\n")


# Real-sample extent (from the raw sample map, section 1.3), not the
# wider raster/buffer extent used for the actual computation - keeps
# these maps showing the area the samples actually span, rather than
# pulling in extra coastline the buffer margin reaches but no sample
# does.
pad_display_x <- 0.10 * (bb_raw[["xmax"]] - bb_raw[["xmin"]])
pad_display_y <- 0.10 * (bb_raw[["ymax"]] - bb_raw[["ymin"]])
display_xlim <- c(bb_raw[["xmin"]] - pad_display_x, bb_raw[["xmax"]] + pad_display_x)
display_ylim <- c(bb_raw[["ymin"]] - pad_display_y, bb_raw[["ymax"]] + pad_display_y)

# By default, reuse the location-statistic clusters. A display override only
# changes these dots; genotype groups and the empirical distance mask stay
# unchanged. Dot positions average unique member sites, counts include all
# member individuals, and values average the WINDOW surface at individuals.
# This is not the direct pooled-genotype statistic used in location analysis.
# Prepare counts and values together before choosing the dot-size mode.
gd_at_point <- terra::extract(wgd[[gd_layer_name]], coords_v_mollweide)[[gd_layer_name]]
# Reuse the hierarchy; only a different display threshold needs another cut.
plot_site_cluster_id <- if (CLUSTER_SAMPLE_POINTS_KM == 0) seq_len(nrow(site_coords)) else
  if (CLUSTER_SAMPLE_POINTS_KM == CLUSTER_VARIANCE_POINTS_KM) site_cluster_id else
  if (nrow(site_coords) > 1L) cutree(site_tree, h = CLUSTER_SAMPLE_POINTS_KM) else 1L
plot_location_id <- unname(plot_site_cluster_id[sample_site_index])
plot_cluster_ids <- as.character(sort(unique(plot_site_cluster_id)))
sample_point_counts <- data.frame(
  Longitude = unname(tapply(site_coords$Longitude, plot_site_cluster_id, mean)[plot_cluster_ids]),
  Latitude = unname(tapply(site_coords$Latitude, plot_site_cluster_id, mean)[plot_cluster_ids]),
  n = as.numeric(table(plot_location_id)[plot_cluster_ids]),
  value = unname(tapply(gd_at_point, plot_location_id, mean, na.rm = TRUE)[plot_cluster_ids]))
# A cluster with no finite plot value gets no point, including count-sized maps.
sample_point_counts <- sample_point_counts[is.finite(sample_point_counts$value), , drop = FALSE]

# If any finite point value is negative (mixed signs or all negative), then absolute values are used for point sizes; heatmaps and analyses keep their signs.
point_values_use_abs <- any(is.finite(sample_point_counts$value) & sample_point_counts$value < 0)
sample_point_counts$size_value <- if (SAMPLE_POINT_SIZE_BY == "value") {
  if (point_values_use_abs) abs(sample_point_counts$value) else sample_point_counts$value
} else {
  sample_point_counts$n
}

# Every plot_with_context() call used to reproject onto a resolution
# project() auto-picked fresh each time. Mollweide is equal-area, so its
# meters-per-degree-longitude shrinks with latitude - a raster that's
# uniform in Mollweide meters is NOT uniform in WGS84 degrees, and this
# domain's ~54-66N span is wide enough for that mismatch to drift across
# an integer source-to-target ratio at specific latitudes. A single fixed
# template, built once and reused for every layer, removes the per-call
# resolution guess entirely rather than just changing what it guesses.
display_res_deg <- (resolution_m / grd_disagg_factor) / 111320
display_template <- rast(xmin = display_xlim[1], xmax = display_xlim[2],
                          ymin = display_ylim[1], ymax = display_ylim[2],
                          resolution = display_res_deg, crs = "EPSG:4326")


# --- Diagnostic: does the thin-line artifact predate WGS84 reprojection? ---
# terra::plot() renders sample_count directly in its native Mollweide CRS -
# no project(), no geom_tile(), nothing that could introduce a nearest-
# neighbor resampling seam. Compare this against count_map immediately
# below: if the lines are absent here but present there, that confirms the
# artifact comes from plot_with_context()'s reprojection step (project()
# auto-picking a resolution that doesn't hold across this domain's latitude
# span), not from window_gd() or coords_to_raster() upstream.
terra::plot(sample_count, main = "sample_count - native Mollweide (diagnostic, no reprojection)")


# Plotting the sample count layer
count_map <- plot_with_context(sample_count,
  paste0("Sample counts per window - ", region_tag), "sample_count", palette = "viridis")
count_map
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, paste0(output_prefix, "sample_count.png")), count_map,
       width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300)

# # Plotting unmasked pi map
# if (use_weighted_kriging) {
#   unmasked_plot_title <- paste0(study_species, "π-diversity (With Weighted Kriging) - ", region_tag, ", unmasked (land excluded only)")

# } else {
#   unmasked_plot_title <- paste0(study_species, "π-diversity - ", region_tag, ", unmasked (land excluded only)")
# }

# Plotting unmasked diversity map
unmasked_plot_title <- paste0(study_species, " ", gd_label, if (use_weighted_kriging) " (With Weighted Kriging)" else "",
                              " - ", region_tag, ", unmasked (land excluded only)")

# For chromosome-/gene-filtered runs the title is rebuilt by make_gd_title() (See setup chunk);
# the suffix keeps this map distinguishable from the masked final map.
gd_map_unmasked <- plot_with_context(mgd,
  make_gd_title(unmasked_plot_title, suffix = ", unmasked (land excluded only)"), gd_label_short)
gd_map_unmasked
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, paste0(output_prefix, "map_unmasked.png")), gd_map_unmasked,
       width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300)

# Plotting the regular pi map after masking
# masked_plot_title is the title for unfiltered runs; chromosome-/gene-filtered
# runs get the make_gd_title() version instead (also used by the sample-point maps below).
masked_plot_title <- paste0(study_species, " ", gd_label, " - ", region_tag, ", masked")
gd_map <- plot_with_context(mgd_honest, make_gd_title(masked_plot_title), gd_label_short)
gd_map
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, paste0(output_prefix, "map.png")), gd_map, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300)

# Plotting the pi map with data points if SHOW_SAMPLE_POINTS == TRUE.
# SAMPLE_POINT_SIZE_BY == "All" generates both the count- and value-sized
# versions as separate files, rather than forcing a single choice.
if (SHOW_SAMPLE_POINTS == TRUE) {
  size_modes <- if (SAMPLE_POINT_SIZE_BY == "All") c("count", "value") else SAMPLE_POINT_SIZE_BY

  for (mode in size_modes) {
    # sample_point_counts$size_value and SAMPLE_POINT_SIZE_BY (read by
    # plot_with_context()'s legend-naming) both need to reflect THIS
    # iteration's mode, not whatever was set when they were first computed
    # earlier - only matters for "All", which runs both modes here, but
    # cheap to always do correctly regardless.
    SAMPLE_POINT_SIZE_BY <- mode
    sample_point_counts$size_value <- if (mode == "value") {
      if (point_values_use_abs) abs(sample_point_counts$value) else sample_point_counts$value
    } else sample_point_counts$n

    # output_prefix already identifies the metric; the ending identifies point sizing.
    suffix <- if (mode == "value") "_by_value" else "_by_count"

    gd_map_sample_points <- plot_with_context(mgd_honest,
      make_gd_title(masked_plot_title), gd_label_short,
      show_points = TRUE)
    print(gd_map_sample_points)  # bare object name doesn't auto-print inside a for loop
    ggsave(file.path(output_dir, paste0(output_prefix, "points", suffix, ".png")),
           gd_map_sample_points, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300)
  }
}


plotting_runtime <- difftime(Sys.time(), start_plotting_time , units = "secs")
message("plotting runtime: ", round(plotting_runtime, 2), " seconds")
print(paste0("plotting runtime: ", round(plotting_runtime, 2), " seconds"))


# Computing script runtime
end_time <- Sys.time()
runtime <- difftime(end_time, start_time, units = "secs")
message("Script runtime: ", round(runtime, 2), " seconds")
print(paste0("Script runtime: ", round(runtime, 2), " seconds"))

# Runtime log - appends one row per run (never overwritten), so runtime
# across different parameter combinations/datasets can be compared later.
# One tab separates the headline total from the per-step breakdown, not a
# fully columnar format - open as text, not spreadsheet software.
runtime_log_path <- file.path(output_dir, "runtime_log.tsv")
log_line <- sprintf(
  "%s: script runtime: %.1f\tread.vcfR runtime=%.1f, wkrig_gd runtime=%.1f, window_gd_runtime=%.1f, distance_masking_runtime=%.1f, plotting_runtime=%.1f",
  output_prefix, as.numeric(runtime), as.numeric(vcf_runtime), as.numeric(wkrig_gd_runtime), as.numeric(window_gd_runtime), as.numeric(distance_masking_runtime), as.numeric(plotting_runtime)
)
log_line <- paste0(log_line, ", grid_engine=", if (grid_efficiency) "optimized" else "native",
                   ", grid_cells=", terra::ncell(lyr_agg), ", grid_min_cells=", grid_min_cells)
cat(log_line, "\n", file = runtime_log_path, append = TRUE, sep = "")
if (diagnostic_run) wingen_helpers$write_diagnostic_timings(output_dir, output_prefix)
```

# 7. Gene Summary Statistics
```{r 7. Gene Summary Statistics}
# ==========================================================================
# Per-gene summary statistics for the gene catalog
# ==========================================================================
# Relies on vcf, coords_file_df, rows_with_na, wgd_confident, min_n_samples_per_calc and output_dir
#
# Checked against the wingen v2.2.0 docs (reference manual + vignette):
#   - the wingen vignette states directly that the dosage matrix used for
#     stat = "pi" has individuals as rows, and hierfstat::pi.dosage()'s own
#     docs describe its `dos` argument the same way (an ni x nl matrix) -
#     so row-wise subsetting in section 4 is the right orientation. Kept
#     as a stopifnot() below rather than just a comment, so a future
#     change to either package fails loudly instead of silently.
#
# Four things are fixed below rather than merely flagged (see the comment
# at each for the reasoning):
#   1. Section 2 now reads from wgd_confident instead of wgd - window_gd()
#      already turns any under-supported window into NA via min_n, so
#      re-filtering by min_n_samples_per_calc here was a no-op sitting
#      next to is.na(), not a second, stricter cut. wgd_confident is the
#      object built earlier for kriging that actually applies the
#      stricter, diagnostic-derived cutoff (minval_sample_count).
#   2. Section 3's "latitude" is actually Mollweide-projected northing in
#      metres (wgd lives in world_crs, not WGS84 - see window_gd()'s own
#      docs on why). The reliable cells' centroids get reprojected to
#      true latitude before calculating their Pearson correlation.
#   3. n_pruned_coord_mismatch now reads nrow(rows_with_na) - already
#      computed earlier in the document - instead of n_unmatched, which
#      only counts samples with no matching coordinate row at all and
#      misses ones that matched a row with a genuinely missing lat/long.
#   4. sample_order can go stale relative to vcf by the time this chunk
#      runs: the coordinate-pruning chunk removes samples from vcf without
#      updating sample_order (the later, optional ROI_ACTIVE block does
#      update it, which is what made this worth checking rather than
#      assuming). current_samples is recomputed fresh from vcf here
#      instead, so section 4 can't drift out of sync with whichever
#      pruning path actually ran for a given gene.
#

# Section 4b:
# Reads off the window surface instead of raw genotypes.
# Mean and median statistics is also included since variance only tells the spread of the diversity metric used, 
# it does however not tell you if the diversity is high or low.

if (compute_genetic_diversity_statistics == TRUE) {
  library(vcfR)
  library(hierfstat)
  library(terra)
  library(jsonlite)

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 1. Individuals, variants, pruning breakdown
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------
  # n_individuals_input intentionally keeps using the ORIGINAL sample_order
  # from load-vcf (before this document prunes anything) - it's meant to
  # answer "how many individuals did we start with", not "how many are left
  # now", so its possible staleness relative to vcf is exactly the point here.
  n_individuals_input <- length(sample_order)
  n_variants <- nrow(vcf@fix)

  # rows_with_na already exists from the coordinate-pruning chunk earlier in
  # the document and covers both cases excluded there: samples with no
  # matching coordinate row at all, and samples that matched a row whose
  # Latitude/Longitude were themselves genuinely missing. n_unmatched alone
  # (from load-coords) only counts the first of those two.
  n_pruned_coord_mismatch <- nrow(rows_with_na)

  # Recomputed fresh from vcf rather than read from sample_order - see the
  # header note on why sample_order alone isn't reliable at this point in
  # the document.
  current_samples <- colnames(vcf@gt)[-1]

  # "VCF error" pruning - individuals with too
  # much missing genotype data at *this gene's own* variant sites
  # specifically (nothing upstream of this Rmd currently checks missingness
  # at the individual level, so this is a new check, not a duplicate of
  # existing QC). 
  gt_matrix <- extract.gt(vcf, element = "GT")
  missing_rate <- apply(gt_matrix, 2, function(col) mean(col %in% c(NA, "./.", ".|.")))

  # Picking this the same way minval_sample_count itself was picked earlier
  # in the document - from the real distribution, not a guess. Worth
  # uncommenting the line below once to look at missing_rate's actual spread
  # across a handful of genes before trusting 0.5 (or whatever replaces it)
  # across the whole catalog.
  # hist(missing_rate, breaks = 20)
  vcf_error_threshold <- 0.5  # placeholder judgment call, not derived from anything yet
  n_pruned_vcf_error <- sum(missing_rate > vcf_error_threshold)

  # Note: this counts how many individuals WOULD fail the threshold above,
  # but doesn't currently remove them from current_samples/dosage before
  # section 4 - matching what the original version of this script did. If
  # "pruned" is meant to also exclude them from the per-location pi calc
  # below, current_samples would need `setdiff(current_samples,
  # names(missing_rate)[missing_rate > vcf_error_threshold])` added here.
  # So "retained" here means "passed the missingness check", NOT "was the only individuals used": every individual in
  # current_samples still goes into both the window and the location statistic. The number actually used is written
  # to the JSON as n_individuals$used_for_gd. Leaving them in is defensible - the per-SNP functions count, SNP by
  # SNP, only the individuals that have a genotype there, so an individual with 60% missing SNPs still contributes at the other
  # 40%. Removing them would have to happen before BOTH window_gd() and the location statistic, or the two
  # approaches would use different individuals.
  n_individuals_retained <- length(current_samples) - n_pruned_vcf_error

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. Overall spatial variance (pi-variance check)
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Raw (non-kriged) per-window values only, from cells with enough real samples nearby.
  # for this number:

  # wgd_confident[[gd_layer_name]], not wgd[[gd_layer_name]] re-filtered by
  # min_n_samples_per_calc: window_gd()'s own min_n already turned any
  # window below that count into NA before wgd ever existed, so re-applying
  # the same threshold here doesn't add a second, stricter cut - it's a
  # no-op alongside is.na(). wgd_confident is the object built earlier
  # (krige chunk) specifically to apply the real, diagnostic-derived cutoff
  # (minval_sample_count) - reusing it here means this number and the
  # kriging input are held to the same bar, with only one place that bar is
  # ever set. Naming by layer (gd_layer_name), not position ([[1]]), also matches how
  # the rest of the document already treats wgd/wgd_confident.

  gd_layer <- wgd_confident[[gd_layer_name]]
  gd_values <- terra::values(gd_layer)
  reliable <- !is.na(gd_values)

  gd_variance_raw_windows <- var(gd_values[reliable])
  gd_mean_raw_windows <- mean(gd_values[reliable])
  gd_median_raw_windows <- median(gd_values[reliable])
  gd_min_raw_windows <- min(gd_values[reliable])
  gd_max_raw_windows <- max(gd_values[reliable])
  # Store abs(mean) for every defined mean; the catalog controls column visibility.
  gd_abs_mean_raw_windows <- abs(gd_mean_raw_windows)

  # (A per-sample version of this - the same confident surface read off at
  # each individual's own coordinate instead of per grid cell - was tried
  # here and removed, not just left unused: a tight group of individuals
  # extracts nearly-identical values that then each count as their own
  # point in the variance, over-weighting wherever sampling effort
  # happened to be dense rather than representing the study area evenly -
  # compounding the clustered-sampling problem above rather than avoiding
  # it. Section 4b below is the version of this idea that actually holds
  # up: same surface, but one point per population/cluster instead of one
  # per individual.)

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 3. Window correlations with latitude and environmental gradients
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Signed Pearson r describes the strength and direction of the window
  # association. These overlapping windows provide a descriptive reference;
  # the neutral simulation comparisons use the per-location statistics.
  # The window grid is Mollweide-projected, so its centroids are transformed
  # to WGS84 to obtain latitude in degrees.

  window_correlation <- function(y, x) {
    keep <- is.finite(y) & is.finite(x)
    y <- y[keep]
    x <- x[keep]
    if (length(y) < 2L || length(unique(y)) < 2L || length(unique(x)) < 2L) {
      return(NA_real_)
    }
    unname(stats::cor(y, x, method = "pearson"))
  }

  cell_xy <- terra::xyFromCell(gd_layer, which(reliable))
  cell_pts <- terra::vect(cell_xy, type = "points", crs = terra::crs(gd_layer))
  cell_pts_wgs84 <- terra::project(cell_pts, "EPSG:4326")
  lat_values <- terra::crds(cell_pts_wgs84)[, "y"]

  gd_latitude_r <- window_correlation(gd_values[reliable], lat_values)

  if (USE_COPERNICUS_MARINE) {
      # --------------------------------------------------------------------
      # 3b. Cell-level Pearson correlation, same footprint as the GD windows
      # --------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Reuse the cell centroids from the latitude correlation to extract
      # each environmental predictor. Same cells, same CRS (env layers are in
      # world_crs from section 2.6, so no reprojection needed here, unlike lat).
      # Each correlation starts with the same reliable cells, then excludes
      # pairs whose diversity or predictor value is missing or non-finite.
      env_at_cell_salinity    <- terra::extract(env_salinity,    cell_pts, ID = FALSE)[[1]]
      env_at_cell_temp_winter <- terra::extract(env_temp_winter, cell_pts, ID = FALSE)[[1]]
      env_at_cell_temp_summer <- terra::extract(env_temp_summer, cell_pts, ID = FALSE)[[1]]
      env_at_cell_chl_log     <- terra::extract(env_chl_log,     cell_pts, ID = FALSE)[[1]]

      gd_salinity_r <- window_correlation(gd_values[reliable], env_at_cell_salinity)
      gd_temp_winter_r <- window_correlation(gd_values[reliable], env_at_cell_temp_winter)
      gd_temp_summer_r <- window_correlation(gd_values[reliable], env_at_cell_temp_summer)
      gd_chl_log_r <- window_correlation(gd_values[reliable], env_at_cell_chl_log)
      if (ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED) {
        env_at_cell_oxygen <- terra::extract(env_oxygen, cell_pts, ID = FALSE)[[1]]
        gd_oxygen_r <- window_correlation(gd_values[reliable], env_at_cell_oxygen)
      }
      if (ENV_CURRENT_SPEED_ENABLED) {
        env_at_cell_current_speed <- terra::extract(env_current_speed, cell_pts, ID = FALSE)[[1]]
        gd_current_speed_r <- window_correlation(gd_values[reliable], env_at_cell_current_speed)
      }
  }
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 4. Per-location variance (nearby sites binned together)
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Each distinct sampling site is here considered as a small population on which the population-based genetic diversity statistic (i.e pi) is computed directly on (rather than using the rolling window-based approach in window_gd().
  # The nucleotide diversity computation is here using wingen's own vcf_to_dosage() + hierfstat::pi.dosage(), the
  # same formula wingen uses internally for "pi".
  #
  # Reuse the complete-linkage groups prepared once in section 1.2.1.
  coords_file_df$variance_cluster_id <- sample_location_id

  # Per-location values are computed directly from these individuals' genotypes.
  # pi, biallelic_richness, theta and tajimas_d use a DOSAGE matrix: individuals in rows, markers in columns; 0 = ref/ref, 1 = ref/alt, 2 = alt/alt, NA = missing.
  # Ho uses Wingen's HETEROZYGOSITY matrix with the same row/column layout: 0/FALSE = homozygous, 1/TRUE = heterozygous, NA = missing. It does not preserve which homozygous allele was present, because Ho only counts heterozygotes.
  # Only the D/theta window_general branch created dosage_matrix above, before computing its windows, so those metrics can reuse that exact input here.
  # For pi/Ho/richness, window_gd converted internally; it did NOT create a dosage_matrix variable in this script. Convert here using gd_input_from_vcf, whose explicit Ho branch selects the heterozygosity matrix instead of dosage.
  if (gd_uses_general) {
    gd_input <- dosage_matrix
  } else {
    gd_input <- gd_input_from_vcf(vcf, gd_stat, current_samples)
  }
  # Row IDs must stay in VCF order: a mismatched genotype/coordinate row could silently assign a statistic to the wrong location. The converter also checks dimensions. Stop on a changed ordering rather than attach incorrect IDs.
  stopifnot(identical(rownames(gd_input), current_samples))


  # Whether the per-location values are rarefied is decided by location_rarify (LOCATION_RARIFY in config.yaml, resolved near the top of this file):
  #   FALSE - each location's value is computed from ALL its individuals: deterministic, nothing random, and the most precise. Right for pi (hierfstat::pi.dosage() uses the per-SNP estimator 2p(1-p) * 2n/(2n-1)) and for Ho (a mean of observed heterozygosity): both have an expected value that does not depend on how many individuals a location has - only their precision does. The price: locations differ in precision (a 5-individual location is noisier than a 150-individual one), which inflates the across-location variance ("Var") somewhat.
  #   TRUE  - a location with more than rarify_n individuals is sub-sampled rarify_n_iterations times at rarify_n individuals and the draws averaged, exactly like window_gd() does per window. This reduces differences in sample size; small clusters still use all individuals, and missingness can also leave differences in precision. The original reason for rarefying them here: a bigger cluster would otherwise give a more precise estimate than a small one purely from sample size, inflating the variance computed ACROSS locations for reasons that have nothing to do with biology. It is especially relevant for biallelic_richness, which grows with sample size. The price: with rarify_n = 4 every location rests on 4 individuals per draw, so the values are far noisier and change with the seed, which weakens every location-level R2 / r / p. For regressions the better remedy for unequal precision is weighting by individual per location (columns n_individuals in the per-location TSV), not discarding individual.
  #   "auto" (default) - TRUE for biallelic_richness when USE_RARIFY is on, FALSE otherwise.min_n_samples_per_calc drops a location below that size entirely, same as it does for a raster window; the max(., 2) enforces the pipeline's minimum of two individuals per location; pi.dosage() itself does not impose it.

  # pi_for_cluster <- function(ids) {
  #   ids_in_vcf <- intersect(ids, current_samples)
  #   if (length(ids_in_vcf) < max(min_n_samples_per_calc, 2)) return(NA_real_)

  #   return(hierfstat::pi.dosage(dosage[ids_in_vcf, , drop = FALSE], L = n_variants))

  #   # Revisit this code in the future when biallelic_richness is given as an option
  #   # if (!use_rarify || length(ids_in_vcf) <= rarify_n) {
  #   #   return(hierfstat::pi.dosage(dosage[ids_in_vcf, , drop = FALSE], L = n_variants))
  #   # }
  #   # draws <- replicate(rarify_n_iterations,
  #   #   hierfstat::pi.dosage(dosage[sample(ids_in_vcf, rarify_n), , drop = FALSE], L = n_variants))
  #   # mean(draws)
  # }

  # One sampling plan for individuals, reused for the target and every neutral replicate. This preserves the original location estimator and random draws.
  location_draws <- make_location_draws(cluster_groups, current_samples,
    min_n_samples_per_calc, location_rarify, rarify_n, rarify_n_iterations, seed_value)
  # gd_of uses the same selected metric as the moving windows. Passing that same function and those same individual draws to the neutral model keeps observed and neutral location estimates directly comparable.
  per_location_gd <- location_gd_from_draws(gd_input, location_draws, gd_of,
    na.rm = gd_uses_general)

  n_locations_used <- sum(!is.na(per_location_gd))
  # Keep the calculations visible. A window spanning several locations can contain variation even if each location is fixed and its D is undefined; in that case report NA for the location summary rather than Inf/NaN.
  gd_variance_per_location <- var(per_location_gd, na.rm = TRUE)
  gd_mean_per_location <- if (n_locations_used) mean(per_location_gd, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_
  gd_median_per_location <- if (n_locations_used) median(per_location_gd, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_
  gd_min_per_location <- if (n_locations_used) min(per_location_gd, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_
  gd_max_per_location <- if (n_locations_used) max(per_location_gd, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_
  gd_abs_mean_per_location <- abs(gd_mean_per_location)

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 4b. Window-surface pi at each population's centroid (pairs with 4:
  #     the same populations as above, but reading wgd_confident's
  #     smoothed surface at each one's centroid instead of computing pi
  #     from raw genotypes - lets you compare "what the model estimates
  #     here" against "what the genotypes actually show" for the same
  #     population, gene by gene)
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------
  # This is the fixed version of the per-sample idea removed from section
  # 2: one point per population/cluster here, not one per individual, so
  # a cluster of 20 people contributes the same single point as a cluster
  # of 2 - the reason the per-individual version was a problem doesn't
  # apply when the unit is the same population section 4 already uses.
  # Centroids are computed in the same Mollweide coordinates window_gd()
  # itself used (coords_v_mollweide), not by averaging raw lat/long, so
  # they sit in the same space gd_layer is defined on and don't need a
  # second reprojection.

  mollweide_xy <- as.data.frame(terra::crds(coords_v_mollweide))
  names(mollweide_xy) <- c("x", "y")  # crds() documents x-then-y order; named explicitly rather than assumed
  mollweide_xy$cluster <- coords_file_df$variance_cluster_id
  centroid_xy <- aggregate(cbind(x, y) ~ cluster, data = mollweide_xy, FUN = mean)
  centroid_pts <- terra::vect(as.matrix(centroid_xy[, c("x", "y")]), type = "points",
                               crs = terra::crs(gd_layer))
  centroid_gd <- terra::extract(gd_layer, centroid_pts)[[gd_layer_name]]

  gd_variance_centroid_windows <- var(centroid_gd, na.rm = TRUE)
  gd_mean_centroid_windows <- mean(centroid_gd, na.rm = TRUE)
  gd_median_centroid_windows <- median(centroid_gd, na.rm = TRUE)

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 4c. Population-level fit: per_location_gd ~ environment averaged over
  #     the same individuals pi was computed from (Track B - see section
  #     2.6's intro). One point per population, no window pooling. This is
  #     the direct, simpler test: does mean nucleotide diversity at a site
  #     track that site's salinity/temperature/chlorophyll, using the
  #     genotype-based per_location_gd from section 4 rather than a value
  #     read off a smoothed/interpolated pi surface.
  #
#     Deliberately NOT the cluster centroid (one representative point): complete linkage keeps every pair of
#     sites in a cluster within the cut-off, so the centroid is a fair location, but it would still collapse the
#     members' own environmental values into the value at one point (and for a coastal cluster that point can
#     fall on a masked cell). The line below this comment states the actual rule.
  #     environmental spread. Instead this reuses cluster_groups (section
  #     4) directly and averages each cluster's members' own env_ind_*
  #     values (section 2.6, named by Sample ID) - the population's
  #     predictor is built from the same individuals pi_for_cluster()
  #     pools for its response, at the same resolution, not from a
  #     resampled point that happens to sit somewhere among them.
  #
  #     Unlike pi_for_cluster(), this is NOT restricted to current_samples
  #     - environment doesn't depend on which individuals had a usable
  #     genotype at this particular gene, only on where the population was
  #     actually sampled, so it shouldn't be recomputed gene to gene.
  #
  #     per_location_gd and the values below both come from sapply() over
  #     the exact same cluster_groups list, so they're guaranteed to be in
  #     the same order - no join needed (unlike the earlier centroid
  #     version, which combined two independently-ordered objects and
  #     joined by cluster ID as a defensive measure; that need goes away
  #     entirely once both sides are sapply() over the same list).
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------
  if (USE_COPERNICUS_MARINE) {
      env_for_cluster <- function(ids, env_ind) {
        vals <- env_ind[ids]
        if (all(is.na(vals))) return(NA_real_)
        mean(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
      }
    
      perloc_env_salinity    <- sapply(cluster_groups, env_for_cluster, env_ind = env_ind_salinity)
      perloc_env_temp_winter <- sapply(cluster_groups, env_for_cluster, env_ind = env_ind_temp_winter)
      perloc_env_temp_summer <- sapply(cluster_groups, env_for_cluster, env_ind = env_ind_temp_summer)
      perloc_env_chl_log     <- sapply(cluster_groups, env_for_cluster, env_ind = env_ind_chl_log)
      if (ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED) perloc_env_oxygen <- sapply(cluster_groups, env_for_cluster, env_ind = env_ind_oxygen)
      if (ENV_CURRENT_SPEED_ENABLED) perloc_env_current_speed <- sapply(cluster_groups, env_for_cluster, env_ind = env_ind_current_speed)
    
      perloc_fit_data <- data.frame(
        gd = unname(per_location_gd),
        salinity = unname(perloc_env_salinity), temp_winter = unname(perloc_env_temp_winter),
        temp_summer = unname(perloc_env_temp_summer), chl_log = unname(perloc_env_chl_log)
      )
      if (ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED) perloc_fit_data$oxygen <- unname(perloc_env_oxygen)
      if (ENV_CURRENT_SPEED_ENABLED) perloc_fit_data$current_speed <- unname(perloc_env_current_speed)
    
      fit_perloc_gradient <- function(env_col) {
        keep <- is.finite(perloc_fit_data$gd) & is.finite(perloc_fit_data[[env_col]])
        if (sum(keep) < 3 || sd(perloc_fit_data$gd[keep]) == 0 ||
            sd(perloc_fit_data[[env_col]][keep]) == 0) return(list(r2 = NA_real_, slope = NA_real_))
        fit <- lm(perloc_fit_data$gd[keep] ~ perloc_fit_data[[env_col]][keep])
        list(r2 = summary(fit)$r.squared, slope = unname(coef(fit)[2]))
      }
    
      fit_perloc_salinity    <- fit_perloc_gradient("salinity")
      fit_perloc_temp_winter <- fit_perloc_gradient("temp_winter")
      fit_perloc_temp_summer <- fit_perloc_gradient("temp_summer")
      fit_perloc_chl_log     <- fit_perloc_gradient("chl_log")
    
      perloc_salinity_r2 <- fit_perloc_salinity$r2;       perloc_salinity_slope    <- fit_perloc_salinity$slope
      perloc_temp_winter_r2 <- fit_perloc_temp_winter$r2; perloc_temp_winter_slope <- fit_perloc_temp_winter$slope
      perloc_temp_summer_r2 <- fit_perloc_temp_summer$r2; perloc_temp_summer_slope <- fit_perloc_temp_summer$slope
      perloc_chl_log_r2 <- fit_perloc_chl_log$r2;         perloc_chl_log_slope     <- fit_perloc_chl_log$slope
      if (ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED) {
        fit_perloc_oxygen <- fit_perloc_gradient("oxygen")
        perloc_oxygen_r2 <- fit_perloc_oxygen$r2
        perloc_oxygen_slope <- fit_perloc_oxygen$slope
      }
      if (ENV_CURRENT_SPEED_ENABLED) {
        fit_perloc_current_speed <- fit_perloc_gradient("current_speed")
        perloc_current_speed_r2 <- fit_perloc_current_speed$r2
        perloc_current_speed_slope <- fit_perloc_current_speed$slope
      }

      # >>> [location-stats] ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # n, signed Pearson r with an analytic 95% confidence interval (Fisher z-transform - this is what cor.test()
      # returns; no bootstrapping needed), the p-value of that same test, and Spearman rho as a rank-based check.
      # CAVEAT: the CI and p-value assume the n locations are independent. Neighbouring coastal locations are not
      # (spatial autocorrelation), so read them as optimistic until a spatially-aware test is added.
      # Switch off: WRITE_LOCATION_STATS: FALSE in config.yaml (wingen_params).
      if (isTRUE(WRITE_LOCATION_STATS)) {
        location_stats <- function(env_col) {
          location_association(perloc_fit_data$gd, perloc_fit_data[[env_col]])
        }
        perloc_stats_salinity    <- location_stats("salinity")
        perloc_stats_temp_winter <- location_stats("temp_winter")
        perloc_stats_temp_summer <- location_stats("temp_summer")
        perloc_stats_chl_log     <- location_stats("chl_log")
        if (ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED) perloc_stats_oxygen <- location_stats("oxygen")
        if (ENV_CURRENT_SPEED_ENABLED) perloc_stats_current_speed <- location_stats("current_speed")
      }
      # <<< [location-stats] ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
}
  # Observed latitude statistics are available with Copernicus on or off.
  perloc_latitude <- unname(vapply(cluster_groups, function(ids)
    mean(coords_file_df$Latitude[match(ids, coords_file_df$`Sample ID`)]), numeric(1)))
  if (isTRUE(WRITE_LOCATION_STATS)) {
    perloc_stats_latitude <- location_association(per_location_gd, perloc_latitude)
  }
  if (RUN_NEUTRAL_SIM) {
    # Reuse this gene's individuals, clusters, environmental means, estimator
    # and individual rarefaction draws. No maps/kriging are recomputed for nulls.
    neutral_predictors <- list(latitude = perloc_latitude)
    if (USE_COPERNICUS_MARINE) {
      neutral_predictors <- c(neutral_predictors, list(salinity = unname(perloc_env_salinity),
        temp_summer = unname(perloc_env_temp_summer), temp_winter = unname(perloc_env_temp_winter),
        chl_log = unname(perloc_env_chl_log)))
      if (ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED) neutral_predictors$oxygen <- unname(perloc_env_oxygen)
      if (ENV_CURRENT_SPEED_ENABLED) neutral_predictors$current_speed <- unname(perloc_env_current_speed)
    }
    min_valid_fraction <- as.numeric(Sys.getenv("NEUTRAL_MIN_VALID_FRACTION", unset = "0.9"))
    if (!is.finite(min_valid_fraction) || min_valid_fraction <= 0 || min_valid_fraction > 1) {
      stop("NEUTRAL_MIN_VALID_FRACTION must be in (0, 1]")
    }
    # Unset uses the default cutoffs; an explicitly empty value disables them.
    extreme_value_percentiles <- validate_extreme_value_percentiles(strsplit(
      Sys.getenv("NEUTRAL_EXTREME_VALUE_PERCENTILES", unset = "95,99"), ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
    neutral_comparison <- run_neutral_model(neutral_plan_path, neutral_metadata_path,
      input_vcf_file, vcf, current_samples, location_draws, per_location_gd, neutral_predictors,
      gd_stat, gd_of, gd_het_fun, file.path(output_dir, statistics_output_prefix),
      min_valid_fraction, prepared_manifest_path = neutral_prepared_manifest_path,
      extreme_value_percentiles = extreme_value_percentiles)
  }
  # >>> [per-location-tsv] -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Audit trail: one row per location (distance cluster) holding exactly the numbers the location-level fits were computed from (column `gd` = the statistic chosen with gd_stat, so the file has the same layout for all genetic diversity metrics). It lets every downstream analysis (partial R2, spatial autocorrelation, weighting by individuals per location, leave-one-out, checking that the environmental columns are identical across genes) run without re-running the window/kriging step.
  # Written next to the plots in the shared per-chromosome folder; the HTML builder only lists .png files and the aggregator only reads *_gene_summary.json, so it cannot interfere with either.
  # Switch off by setting WRITE_PER_LOCATION_TSV: FALSE in config.yaml (wingen_params).
  if (isTRUE(WRITE_PER_LOCATION_TSV) || (USE_COPERNICUS_MARINE && LINKED_PERCENTILE_ENABLED)) {
    loc_gene_id <- Sys.getenv("vcf_filter_value")
    loc_rows <- function(ids) match(ids, coords_file_df$`Sample ID`)
    per_location_table <- data.frame(
      gene_id       = loc_gene_id,
      cluster_id    = as.integer(names(cluster_groups)),
      n_individuals        = unname(vapply(cluster_groups, length, integer(1))),
      n_individuals_for_gd = unname(vapply(cluster_groups, function(ids) length(intersect(ids, current_samples)), integer(1))),
      lat_mean      = unname(vapply(cluster_groups, function(ids) mean(coords_file_df$Latitude[loc_rows(ids)]),  numeric(1))),
      lon_mean      = unname(vapply(cluster_groups, function(ids) mean(coords_file_df$Longitude[loc_rows(ids)]), numeric(1))),
      gd_stat       = gd_stat,
      gd            = unname(per_location_gd),   # the chosen statistic (gd_stat), one value per location
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    if (USE_COPERNICUS_MARINE) {
      per_location_table$salinity    <- unname(perloc_env_salinity)
      per_location_table$temp_winter <- unname(perloc_env_temp_winter)
      per_location_table$temp_summer <- unname(perloc_env_temp_summer)
      per_location_table$chl_log     <- unname(perloc_env_chl_log)
      if (ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED) per_location_table$oxygen <- unname(perloc_env_oxygen)
      if (ENV_CURRENT_SPEED_ENABLED) per_location_table$current_speed <- unname(perloc_env_current_speed)
      # Per variable: how many of this location's individuals had no raw value in the environmental product (masked coastal cell) and were given a neighbour-filled one (section 2.6).
      for (v in names(env_raw_na_flags)) {
        per_location_table[[paste0("n_individuals_filled_", v)]] <-
          unname(vapply(cluster_groups, function(ids) sum(env_raw_na_flags[[v]][ids], na.rm = TRUE), numeric(1)))
      }
    }
    if (isTRUE(WRITE_PER_LOCATION_TSV)) {
      per_location_path <- file.path(output_dir, paste0(statistics_output_prefix, "_per_location.tsv"))
      write.table(per_location_table, per_location_path, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
      cat("Per-location table written:", per_location_path, "\n")
    }
  }
  # <<< [per-location-tsv] -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  # >>> [environmental-model-agreement-export]
  # environmental_layers was saved BEFORE coastal filling. These are full
  # derived environmental rasters, not interpolation of cluster/sample means.
  agreement_manifest <- file.path(output_dir, paste0(statistics_output_prefix, "_linked_percentile_maps.json"))
  if (USE_COPERNICUS_MARINE && LINKED_PERCENTILE_ENABLED) {
    agreement_map_theme <- ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical",
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 13), plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10))
    agreement_map_guide <- ggplot2::guides(fill = ggplot2::guide_colourbar(direction = "horizontal",
      title.position = "top", barwidth = grid::unit(4, "in"), barheight = grid::unit(.16, "in")))
    agreement_environment_plot <- function(raster, label, unit) plot_with_context(raster, label,
      paste0(label, if (nzchar(unit)) paste0(" (", unit, ")") else "")) +
      ggplot2::labs(subtitle = "Copernicus environmental field", caption = NULL) + agreement_map_theme + agreement_map_guide
    agreement_context <- list(layout = "bottom-colourbar-v2", palette = HEATMAP_COLOR_PALETTE, xlim = display_xlim, ylim = display_ylim,
      display_resolution = display_res_deg, spherical = SPHERICAL_GRID,
      display_grid = list(crs = terra::crs(display_template), extent = as.vector(terra::ext(display_template)), resolution = terra::res(display_template)),
      plot_function = deparse(plot_with_context), theme = ggplot2::theme_get(),
      land = sf::st_as_binary(sf::st_geometry(world_land_wgs84)), land_crs = sf::st_crs(world_land_wgs84)$wkt,
      versions = vapply(c("terra", "sf", "ggplot2"), function(package) as.character(utils::packageVersion(package)), character(1)),
      platform = c(R.version.string, Sys.info()[c("sysname", "machine")]))
    agreement_prefix <- if (gene_catalog_run) paste0(statistics_output_prefix, "_", gd_key, "_") else output_prefix
    agreement_aspect <- diff(display_xlim)*cos(mean(display_ylim)*pi/180)/diff(display_ylim)
    if (!is.finite(agreement_aspect) || agreement_aspect <= 0) agreement_aspect <- 1
    ema_export(per_location_table, environmental_layers,
      gd_map + ggplot2::labs(title = gd_stat, subtitle = "Original Wingen surface", caption = NULL) + agreement_map_theme + agreement_map_guide,
      agreement_environment_plot, output_dir, agreement_prefix, statistics_output_prefix, gd_stat,
      file.path(github_repository_path, "code", "templates", "prediction_agreement.template.html"),
      file.path(if (gene_catalog_run) dirname(output_dir) else output_dir, "environment_layers"),
      agreement_context, CLUSTER_VARIANCE_POINTS_KM, EMA_GD_PROBS, EMA_ENV_BREAKS,
      height = max(4, min(16, 7/agreement_aspect + .8)),
      genetic_summary = list(windows = list(min = gd_min_raw_windows, max = gd_max_raw_windows, mean = gd_mean_raw_windows),
        location = list(min = gd_min_per_location, max = gd_max_per_location, mean = gd_mean_per_location, n = n_locations_used)))
  } else if (file.exists(agreement_manifest)) unlink(agreement_manifest)
  # <<< [environmental-model-agreement-export]

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 5. Assemble and write the per-gene manifest
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Doubles as this gene's "did it actually finish" check, and its contents are the "is this gene worth a closer look" check: one file,both jobs.
  # A catalog filename is gene-ID-prefixed (not a plain "gene_summary.json") because its output_dir is the SHARED per-chromosome folder
  # (results/gene_catalog/{chrom}, set by the Snakefile's outdir_abs);every gene on the same chromosome writes here, so a fixed filename would have every later gene silently overwrite the previous one's entry. This is the actual fix for that: each gene's own ID in its own filename means no two genes on the same chromosome ever target the same path, so there is nothing to race or clobber even when several of that chromosome's genes render concurrently. Standalone filenames instead use statistics_output_prefix, which includes the species/settings/metric, protecting pi, theta and D summaries from overwriting one another.
  # centroid = list(variance = gd_variance_centroid_windows, mean = gd_mean_centroid_windows, median = gd_median_centroid_windows)

  gene_id <- Sys.getenv("vcf_filter_value")

  # Field names of the associations with latitude and environmental gradients. The "window_" fields correlate
  # the statistic's window surface with the gradient, so gd_key (lower-case statistic name, e.g. "pi" or "ho") is part
  # of the name - window_pi_salinity_r, window_ho_salinity_r, ... - which is also what becomes a column header in
  # gene_catalog_summary.tsv. The "location_" fields never carried a statistic name. gd_key rather than
  # gd_label_short because a field name has to stay plain ASCII. build_gene_catalog_html.py rebuilds these same
  # names from gd_stat, so the two have to stay in step.
  gradient_fields <- function(suffix, window_r, location_r2 = NULL, location_slope = NULL) {
    fields <- setNames(list(window_r), paste0("window_", gd_key, "_", suffix, "_r"))
    if (!is.null(location_r2)) {
      location_fields <- list(location_r2, location_slope)
      names(location_fields) <- paste0("location_", suffix, c("_r2", "_slope"))
      fields <- c(fields, location_fields)
    }
    fields
  }

  gene_summary <- list(
    gene_id = gene_id,
    target_type = if (neutral_reference) "neutral_pool" else "gene",
    # Which statistic every number in this file is a number OF (gd_stat in config.yaml). Written into each gene's own
    # file so it travels with the data: aggregate_gene_summaries.py refuses to put two statistics into one catalog,
    # and build_gene_catalog_html.py takes its column labels from these three fields.
    gd_stat = gd_stat,
    gd_label = gd_label,
    gd_label_short = gd_label_short,
    n_variants = n_variants,
    n_locations_used = n_locations_used,
    n_individuals_vcf = list(initial = n_individuals_input, retained = n_individuals_retained, vcf_error = n_pruned_vcf_error, coords_mismatch = n_pruned_coord_mismatch),

    windows = list(variance = gd_variance_raw_windows, mean = gd_mean_raw_windows, abs_mean = gd_abs_mean_raw_windows,
                   median = gd_median_raw_windows, min = gd_min_raw_windows, max = gd_max_raw_windows),
    location = list(variance = gd_variance_per_location, mean = gd_mean_per_location, abs_mean = gd_abs_mean_per_location,
                    median = gd_median_per_location, min = gd_min_per_location, max = gd_max_per_location),
    latitude = gradient_fields("latitude", gd_latitude_r)
  )

  if (USE_COPERNICUS_MARINE) {
      # Track A (window_*) - cell-level, same window footprint as the statistic/latitude above.
      # Track B (location_*) - population-level, each cluster's environment averaged over its own member individuals.
      gene_summary$salinity          <- gradient_fields("salinity",    gd_salinity_r,    perloc_salinity_r2,    perloc_salinity_slope)
      gene_summary$water_temp_summer <- gradient_fields("temp_summer", gd_temp_summer_r, perloc_temp_summer_r2, perloc_temp_summer_slope)
      gene_summary$water_temp_winter <- gradient_fields("temp_winter", gd_temp_winter_r, perloc_temp_winter_r2, perloc_temp_winter_slope)
      gene_summary$chlorophyll_a_log <- gradient_fields("chl_log",     gd_chl_log_r,     perloc_chl_log_r2,     perloc_chl_log_slope)
      if (ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED) {
        gene_summary$oxygen <- gradient_fields("oxygen", gd_oxygen_r, perloc_oxygen_r2, perloc_oxygen_slope)
      }
      if (ENV_CURRENT_SPEED_ENABLED) {
        gene_summary$current_speed <- gradient_fields("current_speed", gd_current_speed_r,
          perloc_current_speed_r2, perloc_current_speed_slope)
      }
  }

  # >>> [json-extras] ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Everything between the >>> / <<< markers is additive: it only ADDS fields to gene_summary. Each part has its own guard, so removing or disabling one never affects the others (or the original fields above).

  # (a) individuals actually used for the statistic. n_individuals$retained only SUBTRACTS the >50%-missing individuals from the count; they are NOT removed from the calculation (the per-SNP functions handle missing genotypes).
  gene_summary$n_individuals$used_for_gd <- length(current_samples)

  # (b) Coastal NA fill (section 2.6): how many individuals had no raw value in the environmental product (their cell was masked) and were given a neighbour-filled value, and how many still had none after filling.
  if (USE_COPERNICUS_MARINE && exists("env_before_na") && exists("env_after_na")) {
    gene_summary$env_quality <- c(
      list(n_individuals_total = nrow(coords_file_df)),
      setNames(as.list(unname(env_before_na)), paste0("n_individuals_filled_", names(env_before_na))),
      setNames(as.list(unname(env_after_na)),  paste0("n_individuals_missing_after_fill_", names(env_after_na)))
    )
  }

  # (c) Location-level statistics (section 4c): n, signed r, analytic 95% CI, p, Spearman rho. Written INTO the existing covariate structs so they flatten to e.g. salinity_location_salinity_r in the TSV/duckdb.
  #     Switch off: WRITE_LOCATION_STATS: FALSE in config.yaml (wingen_params).
  if (USE_COPERNICUS_MARINE && isTRUE(WRITE_LOCATION_STATS) && exists("perloc_stats_salinity")) {
    stats_fields <- function(suffix, st) {
      setNames(list(st$n, st$r, st$r_ci_lo, st$r_ci_hi, st$p, st$rho),
               paste0("location_", suffix, c("_n", "_r", "_r_ci_lo", "_r_ci_hi", "_p", "_rho")))
    }
    gene_summary$salinity          <- c(gene_summary$salinity,          stats_fields("salinity",    perloc_stats_salinity))
    gene_summary$water_temp_summer <- c(gene_summary$water_temp_summer, stats_fields("temp_summer", perloc_stats_temp_summer))
    gene_summary$water_temp_winter <- c(gene_summary$water_temp_winter, stats_fields("temp_winter", perloc_stats_temp_winter))
    gene_summary$chlorophyll_a_log <- c(gene_summary$chlorophyll_a_log, stats_fields("chl_log",     perloc_stats_chl_log))
    if (ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED) gene_summary$oxygen <- c(gene_summary$oxygen, stats_fields("oxygen", perloc_stats_oxygen))
    if (ENV_CURRENT_SPEED_ENABLED) gene_summary$current_speed <- c(gene_summary$current_speed,
      stats_fields("current_speed", perloc_stats_current_speed))
  }

  if (isTRUE(WRITE_LOCATION_STATS)) {
    st <- perloc_stats_latitude
    gene_summary$latitude <- c(gene_summary$latitude, setNames(
      list(st$n, st$r, st$r_ci_lo, st$r_ci_hi, st$p, st$rho),
      paste0("location_latitude", c("_n", "_r", "_r_ci_lo", "_r_ci_hi", "_p", "_rho"))))
  }
  if (RUN_NEUTRAL_SIM) {
    groups_by_variable <- c(latitude = "latitude", salinity = "salinity", temp_summer = "water_temp_summer",
      temp_winter = "water_temp_winter", chl_log = "chlorophyll_a_log",
      oxygen = "oxygen", current_speed = "current_speed")
    for (variable in names(neutral_comparison$fields)) {
      fields <- neutral_comparison$fields[[variable]]
      names(fields) <- paste0("location_", variable, "_", names(fields))
      group <- groups_by_variable[[variable]]
      gene_summary[[group]] <- c(gene_summary[[group]], fields)
    }
    # Scalar fields only, so the existing DuckDB/TSV flattener remains valid.
    info <- neutral_comparison$metadata
    gene_summary$neutral_model <- list(status = info$status, n_available = info$n_available,
      n_excluded_overlap = info$n_excluded_overlap, n_variants_matched = info$n_variants,
      technical_replicates_requested = info$technical_replicates_requested, seed = info$seed,
      pool_sha256 = info$pool_sha256, comparison = "upper_tail_absolute_correlation",
      min_valid_fraction = min_valid_fraction, common_individual_draws = TRUE,
      extreme_value_percentiles = info$extreme_value_percentiles,
      gd_stat = info$gd_stat, gd_dosage_missing_policy = info$gd_dosage_missing_policy,
      pool_validation = info$pool_validation)
    if (!is.null(info$prepared_manifest_md5)) gene_summary$neutral_model$prepared_manifest_md5 <- info$prepared_manifest_md5
    gene_summary$neutral_model$n_markers_matched <- info$pool_n_matched
  }

  # The optional reference is the catalog row formerly named All_neutral_markers.
  # A debug pool limit changes the sampling population for ALL neutral comparisons.
  pool_manifest_path <- Sys.getenv("NEUTRAL_POOL_MANIFEST", unset = "")
  pool_info <- if (nzchar(pool_manifest_path)) jsonlite::fromJSON(pool_manifest_path) else NULL
  if (!is.null(pool_info)) gene_summary$neutral_sampling_pool <- list(
    debug_limit_requested = TRUE, limited = !isTRUE(pool_info$all_markers),
    source_n_markers = pool_info$pool_n_records, n_markers = pool_info$selected_n_records,
    max_markers = pool_info$max_markers, seed = pool_info$seed,
    source_pool = pool_info$source_pool, selected_sites_sha256 = pool_info$selected_sites_sha256)

  if (neutral_reference) {
    reference_manifest_path <- Sys.getenv("NEUTRAL_REFERENCE_MANIFEST", unset = "")
    reference_info <- if (nzchar(reference_manifest_path)) jsonlite::fromJSON(reference_manifest_path) else NULL
    if (!is.null(reference_info) && !identical(as.numeric(reference_info$selected_n_records), as.numeric(n_variants)))
      stop("Neutral reference VCF marker count differs from its preparation manifest")
    all_sampling_pool_markers <- is.null(reference_info) || isTRUE(reference_info$all_markers)
    all_source_markers <- all_sampling_pool_markers && (is.null(pool_info) || isTRUE(pool_info$all_markers))
    gene_summary$neutral_pool <- list(
      all_markers = all_source_markers, all_sampling_pool_markers = all_sampling_pool_markers,
      n_markers = n_variants,
      source_vcf = normalizePath(input_vcf_file, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE),
      scope = if (all_source_markers) "entire source neutral pool; gene_scope does not apply" else
        if (all_sampling_pool_markers) "entire debug-limited sampling pool; not all source markers" else
          "seeded reference subset of the configured sampling pool; gene_scope does not apply",
      interpretation = "pooled neutral reference; not a marker-count-matched null replicate")
    if (!is.null(reference_info)) gene_summary$neutral_pool <- c(gene_summary$neutral_pool, list(
      pool_n_markers = reference_info$pool_n_records, max_markers = reference_info$max_markers,
      seed = reference_info$seed, source_pool = reference_info$source_pool,
      sampling = reference_info$sampling, selected_sites_sha256 = reference_info$selected_sites_sha256))
  }

  # (d) The settings that produced this gene's numbers (provenance). Switch off: WRITE_RUN_SETTINGS: FALSE.
  if (isTRUE(WRITE_RUN_SETTINGS)) {
    gene_summary$run_settings <- list(
      gd_stat = gd_stat, seed = seed_value, use_rarify = use_rarify, location_rarify = location_rarify,
      domain_type = domain_type, grid_efficiency = grid_efficiency,
      grid_min_cells = as.character(grid_min_cells), kriging_chunk_cells = kriging_chunk_cells,
      diagnostic_run = diagnostic_run, preview_windows = preview_windows,
      grid_validate = isTRUE(attr(wingen_functions, "validation")),
      gd_dosage_missing_policy = if (gd_uses_general) gd_dosage_missing_policy else NA_character_,
      rarify_n = rarify_n, rarify_n_iterations = rarify_n_iterations,
      min_n_samples_per_calc = min_n_samples_per_calc, wdim = wdim_value, fact = fact_value,
      resolution_km = resolution_m / 1e3, cluster_variance_km = CLUSTER_VARIANCE_POINTS_KM,
      cluster_sample_points_km = CLUSTER_SAMPLE_POINTS_KM, spacing_cluster_km = SPACING_CLUSTER_KM,
      use_weighted_kriging = use_weighted_kriging, nmax_neighbours = nmax_neighbours,
      environmental_agreement_export = LINKED_PERCENTILE_ENABLED,
      environmental_agreement_fit_location = "R_before_export",
      environmental_agreement_fitting_engine = "R",
      environmental_agreement_genetic_probs = EMA_GD_PROBS,
      environmental_agreement_environment_breaks = EMA_ENV_BREAKS
    )
    if (USE_COPERNICUS_MARINE) {
      gene_summary$run_settings <- c(gene_summary$run_settings, list(
        env_preset = ENV_PRESET,
        env_physics_product = ENV_PHYSICS_PRODUCT, env_physics_years = paste(env_years_physics, collapse = "-"),
        env_chl_product = ENV_CHL_PRODUCT,         env_chl_years = paste(env_years_chl, collapse = "-"),
        env_depth_m = ENV_DEPTH_M, env_oxygen_enabled = ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED,
        env_current_speed_enabled = ENV_CURRENT_SPEED_ENABLED
      ))
      if (ENV_OXYGEN_ENABLED) {
        gene_summary$run_settings <- c(gene_summary$run_settings, list(
          env_oxygen_product = ENV_OXYGEN_PRODUCT, env_oxygen_layer = ENV_OXYGEN_LAYER,
          env_oxygen_variable = ENV_OXYGEN_VARIABLE, env_oxygen_years = paste(env_years_oxygen, collapse = "-"),
          env_oxygen_depth_m = ENV_OXYGEN_DEPTH_M, env_oxygen_units = "mmol/m^3"
        ))
      }
      if (ENV_CURRENT_SPEED_ENABLED) {
        gene_summary$run_settings <- c(gene_summary$run_settings, list(
          env_current_speed_definition = sprintf("mean(sqrt(%s^2 + %s^2)) over monthly mean components",
            ENV_CURRENT_EASTWARD_VAR, ENV_CURRENT_NORTHWARD_VAR),
          env_current_speed_units = "m/s", env_current_speed_layer = ENV_PHYSICS_LAYER,
          env_current_eastward_variable = ENV_CURRENT_EASTWARD_VAR,
          env_current_northward_variable = ENV_CURRENT_NORTHWARD_VAR
        ))
      }
    }
  }
  # <<< [json-extras] ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  jsonlite::write_json(gene_summary, file.path(output_dir, paste0(statistics_output_prefix, "_gene_summary.json")),
                        auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 8, na = "null")  # na = "null": NA becomes JSON null (the default writes the STRING "NA", which turns a whole DuckDB column into text)
  print(file.path(output_dir, paste0(statistics_output_prefix, "_gene_summary.json")))
  
}

```
